title.zh: 卷五十一 列傳第三十二 裴叔業 崔慧景 張欣泰
title.en: Volume 51 Biographies 32: Pei Shuye, Cui Huijing, Zhang Xintai
title.raw: 卷五十一 列傳第三十二 裴叔業 崔慧景 張欣泰 Volume 51 Biographies 32: Pei Shuye, Cui Huijing, Zhang Xintai

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷五十一‧列傳第三十二

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 51, Biographies 32
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 51, Biographies 32

sentences.zh: 裴叔業 崔慧景 張欣泰

translations.literal: Pei Shuye, Cui Huijing, Zhang Xintai
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye, Cui Huijing, and Zhang Xintai

sentences.zh: 上初卽位，羣下各獻讜言。

translations.literal: When the emperor first ascended the throne, all officials submitted remonstrances and advice.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne, officials throughout the court submitted remonstrances and advice.

sentences.zh: 二年，叔業上疏曰：「成都沃壤，四塞爲固，古稱一人守隘，萬夫趑趄。

translations.literal: In the second year, Shuye submitted a memorial saying: "Chengdu is fertile soil, fortified on all four sides; antiquity says that one man guarding a pass makes ten thousand men hesitate and shrink back.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Shuye submitted a memorial saying: "Chengdu is rich land, sealed off on all four sides; the ancients said that one man holding a defile could make ten thousand men falter and hang back.

sentences.zh: 雍、齊亂於漢世，譙、李寇於晉代，成敗之迹，事載前史。

translations.literal: Yong and Qi were troubled in Han times; Qiao and Li harried in Jin times—the traces of success and failure are recorded in previous histories.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Yong and Qi were thrown into disorder; in Jin times Qiao and Li raided as enemies—the record of victory and defeat is set down in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 頃世以來，綏馭乖術，地惟形勢，居之者異姓，國實武用，鎮之者無兵，致寇掠充斥，賧稅不斷。

translations.literal: In recent generations regulation and control have used wrong methods; the territory has only strategic position—those who hold it are of other surnames, the state relies on military force yet those who garrison have no troops, so raids and plunder fill the land and tribute payments never cease.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times governance has gone awry: the region has nothing but strategic terrain, yet those who hold it are men of other clans; the state depends on arms, yet those who garrison it have no soldiers—so bandit raids fill the land and tribute levies never stop.

sentences.zh: 宜遣帝子之尊，臨撫巴蜀，總益、梁、南秦爲三州刺史。

translations.literal: It would be fitting to send a prince of the imperial house of exalted rank to oversee and pacify Ba-Shu, supervising the three provinces Yi, Liang, and South Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The court should send a prince of the imperial house, one of exalted rank, to oversee Ba-Shu, holding together the three provinces of Yi, Liang, and South Qin.

sentences.zh: 率文武萬人，先啓崏漢，分遣郡戍，皆配精力，搜盪山源，糾虔姦蠹。

translations.literal: Lead ten thousand civil and military officials, first open Min and Han, dispatch the prefectural garrisons all with picked soldiers, scour the mountain valleys, and root out banditry and corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He should lead ten thousand civil and military men, first open the passes at Min and Han, send out the prefectural garrisons all manned with picked troops, scour the mountain country, and punish bandits and corruption.

sentences.zh: 威令旣行，民夷必服。」

translations.literal: Once authority and orders are in force, Chinese and barbarians will surely submit."
translations.idiomatic: Once his authority is established, both Chinese and tribesmen will surely submit."

sentences.zh: 除寧朔將軍，軍主如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North; his post as army commander remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, retaining his post as army commander.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，累至右軍將軍，東中郎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, he rose in successive posts to General of the Right Army and Adviser of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongming he rose through successive posts to General of the Right Army and Adviser of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 叔業早與高宗接事，高宗輔政，厚任叔業以爲心腹，使領軍掩襲諸蕃鎮，叔業盡心用命。

translations.literal: Shuye had long handled affairs for Emperor Ming; when Emperor Ming assisted in government he entrusted Shuye heavily as a trusted confidant, having him lead troops in surprise attacks on the various garrison provinces; Shuye devoted his full effort.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye had long served Emperor Ming in daily business; when Ming assisted in government he relied on Shuye as a trusted confidant and had him lead troops in surprise strikes against the frontier garrisons, and Shuye gave his whole heart to the task.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，虜圍徐州，叔業以軍主隷右衞將軍蕭坦之救援。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, the barbarians besieged Xuzhou; Shuye as army commander served under General of the Right Wei Xiao Tanzhi in the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu the barbarians besieged Xuzhou; Shuye, as army commander, served under General of the Right Wei Xiao Tanzhi in the relief force.

sentences.zh: 叔業攻虜淮柵外二城，剋之，賊衆赴水死甚衆。

translations.literal: Shuye attacked the barbarians' two cities outside the Huai stockade and took them; many of the enemy threw themselves into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye attacked the barbarians' two cities outside the Huai palisade and captured them; a great many of the enemy threw themselves into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 除黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 上以叔業有勳誠，封武昌縣伯，五百戶。

translations.literal: Because Shuye had merit and loyalty, the emperor enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuchang with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shuye had shown merit and loyalty, the emperor enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuchang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍爲持節、督徐州軍事、冠軍將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was also made bearer of the staff, supervisor of Xuzhou military affairs, General Who Exerts Martial Force, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made bearer of the staff, supervisor of Xuzhou military affairs, General Who Exerts Martial Force, and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，虜主寇沔北，上令叔業援雍州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the barbarian lord invaded north of the Han, and the emperor ordered Shuye to aid Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the barbarian lord invaded the region north of the Han, and the emperor ordered Shuye to reinforce Yong province.

sentences.zh: 叔業啓：「北人不樂遠行，唯樂侵伐虜堺，則雍司之賊，自然分張，無勞動民向遠也。」

translations.literal: Shuye petitioned: "Northerners do not like to travel far; they love only to raid the barbarian frontier, then the enemy of Yong and Si will naturally scatter without moving the people on far campaigns."
translations.idiomatic: Shuye petitioned: "The northerners dislike marching far; they love only to strike the barbarian frontier. Then the foes of Yong and Si will scatter of themselves, without moving our people on distant campaigns."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 叔業率軍攻虹城，獲男女四千餘人。

translations.literal: Shuye led the army to attack Hongcheng and captured more than four thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye led his army to attack Hongcheng and took more than four thousand men and women captive.

sentences.zh: 徙督豫州、輔國將軍、豫州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise Yuzhou, made General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yuzhou, bearer of the staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervise Yuzhou, appointed General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yuzhou, bearer of the staff as before.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，叔業領東海太守孫令終、新昌太守劉思效、馬頭太守李僧護等五萬人圍渦陽，虜南兖州所鎮，去彭城百二十里。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Shuye led the Donghai prefect Sun Lingzhong, Xinchang prefect Liu Sixiao, Matou prefect Li Sengfu, and others—fifty thousand men—to besiege Guoyang, garrisoned by the barbarians' Southern Yan province, one hundred twenty li from Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, Shuye led the Donghai prefect Sun Lingzhong, the Xinchang prefect Liu Sixiao, the Matou prefect Li Sengfu, and others—fifty thousand men in all—to besiege Guoyang, which the barbarians held as their Southern Yan provincial seat, one hundred twenty li from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 偽兖州刺史孟表固守拒戰，叔業攻圍之，積所斬級高五丈，以示城內。

translations.literal: The false Inspector of Yanzhou Meng Biao held firm and resisted battle; Shuye besieged him, heaping the heads of those slain to a height of five zhang to show those within the city.
translations.idiomatic: The false Inspector of Yanzhou, Meng Biao, held the city and fought back; Shuye pressed the siege and piled the heads of those he had slain to a height of five zhang, displaying them to those inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 又遣軍主蕭璝、成寶真分攻龍亢戍，卽虜馬頭郡也。

translations.literal: He also sent army commander Xiao Jun and Cheng Baozhen on separate attacks on the Longgeng garrison, which was the barbarians' Matou commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the army commanders Xiao Jun and Cheng Baozhen to attack the Longgeng garrison separately—that being the barbarians' Matou commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 虜閉城自守。

translations.literal: The barbarians shut the city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians shut the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 偽徐州刺史廣陵王率二萬人，騎五千匹，至龍亢，璝等拒戰不敵。

translations.literal: The false Xuzhou Inspector, Prince of Guangling, led twenty thousand men with five thousand horses to Longgeng; Jun and others resisted but could not match them.
translations.idiomatic: The false Inspector of Xuzhou, the Prince of Guangling, came to Longgeng with twenty thousand men and five thousand horses; Jun and the others fought but could not withstand them.

sentences.zh: 叔業三萬餘人助之，數道攻虜。

translations.literal: Shuye with more than thirty thousand men aided them, attacking the barbarians by several routes.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye came to their aid with more than thirty thousand men and attacked the barbarians along several routes.

sentences.zh: 虜新至，營未立，於是大敗。

translations.literal: The barbarians had newly arrived and their camp was not yet established, so they suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians had only just arrived and their camp was not yet set up, so they suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王與數十騎走，官軍追獲其節。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangling fled with several dozen horsemen; government troops pursued and seized his staff of office.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangling fled with several dozen horsemen; government troops pursued and captured his credential staff.

sentences.zh: 虜又遣偽將劉藻、高匆繼至，叔業率軍迎擊破之，再戰，斬首萬級，獲生口三千人，器仗驢馬絹布千萬計。

translations.literal: The barbarians again sent the false generals Liu Zao and Gao Cong in succession; Shuye led troops to meet and defeat them; in a second battle he beheaded ten thousand, captured three thousand alive, and weapons, mounts, silk, and cloth beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians again sent the false generals Liu Zao and Gao Cong in turn; Shuye led troops out to meet and rout them. In a second engagement he beheaded ten thousand, took three thousand alive, and seized weapons, pack animals, silk, and cloth in quantities beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 虜主聞廣陵王敗，遣偽都督王肅、大將軍楊大眼步騎十餘萬救渦陽，叔業見兵盛，夜委軍遁走。

translations.literal: When the barbarian lord heard the Prince of Guangling had been defeated, he sent the false commander Wang Su and Grand General Yang Daoyan with more than one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve Guoyang; Shuye saw their forces were strong and by night abandoned the army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarian lord heard that the Prince of Guangling had been defeated, he sent the false commander Wang Su and the Grand General Yang Daoyan with more than one hundred thousand foot and horse to relieve Guoyang. Shuye saw how strong they were and by night abandoned his army and fled.

sentences.zh: 明日，官軍奔潰，虜追之，傷殺不可勝數，日暮乃止。

translations.literal: The next day government troops scattered in rout; the barbarians pursued, killing and wounding beyond counting until evening when they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the government troops broke and fled; the barbarians pursued them, killing and wounding beyond count, and only at dusk did they halt.

sentences.zh: 叔業還保渦口，上遣使慰勞。

translations.literal: Shuye returned to hold Guokou; the emperor sent envoys to console him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye withdrew to hold Guokou; the emperor sent envoys to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，叔業還鎮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Shuye returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Shuye returned to his commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 少主卽位，誅大臣，京師屢有變發。

translations.literal: When the young emperor took the throne he executed great ministers, and the capital saw disturbances repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: When the young emperor took the throne he put great ministers to death, and the capital was shaken by upheavals again and again.

sentences.zh: 叔業登壽春城北望肥水，謂部下曰：「卿等欲富貴乎？

translations.literal: Shuye mounted the north wall of Shouchun and looked north across the Fei River, saying to his subordinates: "Do you wish for wealth and honor?
translations.idiomatic: Shuye climbed the north wall of Shouchun and gazed north across the Fei River, saying to his officers: "Do you want wealth and rank?

sentences.zh: 我言富貴亦可辦耳。」

translations.literal: What I say—wealth and honor can also be arranged."
translations.idiomatic: What I tell you—wealth and rank can be arranged as well."

sentences.zh: 永元元年，徙督南兖兖徐青冀五州軍事、南兖州刺史，將軍、持節如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he was transferred to supervise the five provinces Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, made Inspector of Nan Yan; general and bearer of the staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan he was transferred to supervise military affairs in the five provinces of Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji and made Inspector of Nan Yan; his rank as general and bearer of the staff remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 叔業見時方亂，不樂居近蕃，朝廷疑其欲反，叔業亦遣使參察京師消息，於是異論轉盛。

translations.literal: Shuye saw the times were in disorder and did not wish to dwell near the capital province; the court suspected he meant to rebel, and Shuye also sent agents to investigate news from the capital—thereupon divergent opinion grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye saw the realm falling into chaos and did not wish to remain near the capital frontier; the court suspected he intended to rebel, and Shuye in turn sent agents to spy on news from the capital—so conflicting reports grew ever louder.

sentences.zh: 叔業兄子植、颺竝爲直閤，殿內驅使。

translations.literal: Shuye's nephews Zhi and Yang were both direct attendants, runners within the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye's nephews Zhi and Yang were both direct attendants, serving as runners within the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 慮禍至，棄母奔壽陽，說叔業以朝廷必見掩襲。

translations.literal: Fearing disaster would come they abandoned their mother and fled to Shouchun, telling Shuye the court would surely send a surprise force to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disaster was coming, they abandoned their mother and fled to Shouchun, telling Shuye that the court would surely send troops in a surprise strike to take him.

sentences.zh: 徐世檦等慮叔業外叛，遣其宗人中書舍人裴長穆宣旨，許停本任。

translations.literal: Xu Shizhi and others, fearing Shuye would rebel outward, sent his clansman Attendant of the Central Secretariat Pei Changmu to announce the decree, permitting him to retain his current post.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shizhi and others, fearing Shuye would defect to the enemy, sent his clansman Pei Changmu, Attendant of the Central Secretariat, to announce the imperial decree allowing him to keep his present post.

sentences.zh: 叔業猶不自安，而植等說之不已，叔業憂懼，問計於梁王，梁王令遣家還都，自然無患。

translations.literal: Shuye was still uneasy, and Zhi and others pressed him without cease; Shuye in worry asked counsel of the Prince of Liang, who told him to send his family back to the capital and naturally there would be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye was still uneasy, and Zhi and the others urged him without end. Troubled, Shuye asked the Prince of Liang for counsel; the prince told him to send his household back to the capital and he would naturally be free of harm.

sentences.zh: 叔業乃遣子芬之等還質京師。

translations.literal: Shuye then sent his son Fenzhi and others back as hostages to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye then sent his son Fenzhi and others back to the capital as hostages.

sentences.zh: 明年，進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: The next year his title was advanced to General Who Exerts Martial Force.
translations.idiomatic: The following year his rank was advanced to General Who Exerts Martial Force.

sentences.zh: 傳叔業反者不已，芬之愈懼，復奔壽春。

translations.literal: Reports that Shuye was rebelling did not stop; Fenzhi grew ever more afraid and again fled to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors that Shuye was rebelling never ceased; Fenzhi grew ever more frightened and fled again to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 於是發詔討叔業，遣護軍將軍崔慧景、征虜將軍豫州刺史蕭懿督水陸衆軍西討，頓軍小峴。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to campaign against Shuye; Protecting Army General Cui Huijing and Conquering Barbarians General and Yuzhou Inspector Xiao Yi were dispatched to supervise land and water forces on a western campaign, halting at Little Xiao mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict went out to campaign against Shuye. Protecting Army General Cui Huijing and Conquering Barbarians General and Inspector of Yuzhou Xiao Yi were ordered to command the land and river forces in a western campaign, halting at Little Xiao mountain.

sentences.zh: 叔業病困，植請救魏虜，送芬之爲質。

translations.literal: Shuye fell gravely ill; Zhi requested aid from the Northern Wei barbarians and sent Fenzhi as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye fell gravely ill; Zhi asked the Northern Wei barbarians for aid and sent Fenzhi as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 叔業尋卒，虜遣大將軍李醜楊大眼二千餘騎入壽春。

translations.literal: Shuye soon died; the barbarians sent Grand General Li Chou and Yang Daoyan with more than two thousand horsemen into Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye soon died; the barbarians sent the Grand General Li Chou and Yang Daoyan with more than two thousand horsemen into Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 初，虜主元宏建武二年至壽春，其下勸攻城。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the second year of Jianwu the barbarian lord Yuan Hong came to Shouchun; his subordinates urged attacking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the second year of Jianwu the barbarian lord Yuan Hong had come to Shouchun; his subordinates urged him to storm the city.

sentences.zh: 宏曰：「不須攻，後當降也。」

translations.literal: Hong said: "No need to attack; later it will surrender of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Hong said: "There is no need to attack; in time it will surrender on its own."

sentences.zh: 植等皆還洛陽。

translations.literal: Zhi and the others all returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and the others all returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景字君山，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Huijing, style Junshan, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing, whose style name was Junshan, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖構，奉朝請。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gou was a court gentleman in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gou was a court gentleman in regular attendance.

sentences.zh: 父系之，州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Xizhi was a provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xizhi served as a provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 慧景初爲國子學生。

translations.literal: Huijing began as a student in the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing began his career as a student in the National University.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始中，歷位至員外郎，稍遷長水校尉，寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Song he rose through posts to Outer Gentleman, then gradually to Colonel of the Long Rivers, General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era of Song he rose through posts to Outer Gentleman, then step by step to Colonel of the Long Rivers and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 太祖在淮陰，慧景與宗人祖思同時自結，太祖欲北渡廣陵，使慧景具船於陶家後渚，事雖不遂，以此見親。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was at Huaiyin, Huijing and his clansman Zusi pledged themselves together at the same time; the Founding Emperor wished to cross north to Guangling and had Huijing prepare boats at the Tao family rear ford—though the affair did not succeed he was drawn close on this account.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor was at Huaiyin, Huijing and his clansman Zusi pledged themselves to him at the same time. The Founding Emperor wished to cross north to Guangling and had Huijing prepare boats at the Tao family rear landing; though the plan did not succeed, he was drawn close on this account.

sentences.zh: 除前軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Front Army [officer].
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the Front Army.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事平，仍出爲武陵王安西司馬、河東太守，使防扞陝西。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair was pacified he went out as Chief Clerk to the Peaceful Western Army of the Prince of Wuling and Prefect of Hedong, sent to defend west of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi's rebellion was put down he went out as Chief Clerk to the Peaceful Western Army of the Prince of Wuling and Prefect of Hedong, charged with defending the region west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 昇明三年，豫章王爲荊州，慧景留爲鎮西司馬，兼諮議，太守如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming the Prince of Yuzhang was made Inspector of Jingzhou; Huijing remained as Chief Clerk of the Suppressing West Army and concurrent adviser, prefect as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shengming the Prince of Yuzhang was made Inspector of Jingzhou; Huijing stayed on as Chief Clerk of the Suppressing West Army with concurrent duties as adviser, retaining his prefecture as before.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，封樂安縣子，三百戶。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor accepted the Mandate he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Le'an with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor received the Mandate, Huijing was enfeoffed as Viscount of Le'an with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 豫章王遣慧景奉表稱慶還京師，太祖召見，加意勞接。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang sent Huijing to deliver the felicitation memorial and return to the capital; the Founding Emperor summoned him and treated him with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang sent Huijing to the capital with a memorial of congratulation; the Founding Emperor summoned him and received him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 轉平西府司馬、南郡內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Pacifying West Army and Interior Minister of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Pacifying West Army and Interior Minister of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 仍遷爲南蠻長史，加輔國將軍，內史如故。

translations.literal: He was soon moved to Chief Clerk of the Southern Barbarians, with additional title General Who Assists the State, interior minister as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Chief Clerk of the Southern Barbarians with the additional title General Who Assists the State, retaining the interior ministry as before.

sentences.zh: 先是蠻府置佐，資用甚輕，至是始重其選。

translations.literal: Previously the barbarian office's aides were lightly supplied—only now was the selection weighted heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the aides of the Southern Barbarians office were lightly provisioned; only now was the post given real weight in selection.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne his title was advanced to General Who Exerts Martial Force.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Huijing's rank was advanced to General Who Exerts Martial Force.

sentences.zh: 在州蓄聚，多獲珍貨。

translations.literal: While in the province he gathered wealth and obtained many rare goods.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the province he amassed wealth and acquired many rare goods.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，以本號還。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming he returned with his present title.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming he returned to court with his present rank.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門郎，領羽林監。

translations.literal: He was moved to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and oversaw the Feathered Forest guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and placed in charge of the Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷隨王東中郎司馬，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Eastern Palace of the Prince of Sui and additional General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Eastern Palace of the Prince of Sui with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、督司州軍事、冠軍將軍、司州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as bearer of the staff, supervisor of Si province military affairs, General Who Exerts Martial Force, and Inspector of Si province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as bearer of the staff, supervisor of Si province military affairs, General Who Exerts Martial Force, and Inspector of Si province.

sentences.zh: 母喪，詔起復本任。

translations.literal: When his mother died an edict recalled him to his former post before mourning was finished.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, an edict ordered him back to his former post before the mourning period had ended.

sentences.zh: 慧景每罷州，輙傾資獻奉，動數百萬，世祖以此嘉之。

translations.literal: Whenever Huijing left a province he poured out his wealth in tribute—several million each time—and Emperor Wu admired him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Huijing left a province he emptied his coffers in tribute to the throne—several million each time—and Emperor Wu praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 九年，以本號徵還，轉太子左率，加通直常侍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was recalled with his present title, transferred to Left Leader of the Heir Apparent's guard and additional Unimpeded Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was recalled with his present rank and transferred to Left Leader of the Heir Apparent's guard with the additional post of Unimpeded Attendant.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷右衞將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to General of the Right Wei and additional Recipient for the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was moved to General of the Right Wei with the additional post of Recipient for the Palace.

sentences.zh: 是時虜將南侵，上出慧景爲持節、督豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡諸軍事、冠軍將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarians were about to invade south; the emperor sent Huijing out as bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in the two commanderies Xiyang of Yuzhou and Runan of Sizhou, General Who Exerts Martial Force, and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the barbarians were poised to invade the south; the emperor sent Huijing out as bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Xiyang commandery of Yuzhou and Runan commandery of Sizhou, General Who Exerts Martial Force, and Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne Huijing's title was advanced to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, Huijing's rank was advanced to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 慧景以少主新立，密與虜交通，朝廷疑懼。

translations.literal: Huijing, seeing the young emperor had newly taken the throne, secretly communicated with the barbarians; the court grew suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing, seeing that the young emperor had only just ascended, secretly opened communications with the barbarians, and the court grew suspicious and uneasy.

sentences.zh: 高宗輔政，遣梁王至壽春安慰之，慧景遣密啓送誠勸進，徵還，爲散騎常侍，左衞將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming assisted in government he sent the Prince of Liang to Shouchun to console him; Huijing sent a secret memorial offering loyalty and urging advancement; recalled, made Unattached Cavalier Attendant and General of the Left Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming assisted in government he sent the Prince of Liang to Shouchun to reassure him; Huijing sent a secret memorial pledging loyalty and urging him to advance. Recalled to court, he was made Unattached Cavalier Attendant and General of the Left Wei.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，虜寇徐、豫，慧景以本官假節向鍾離，受王玄邈節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu the barbarians harried Xu and Yu; Huijing with his present office borrowed the staff and went to Zhongli, subject to Wang Xuamo's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu the barbarians raided Xu and Yu; Huijing, with his present office, borrowed the staff and went to Zhongli, placing himself under Wang Xuamo's command.

sentences.zh: 尋加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he received additional title General Who Exerts Martial Force.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received the additional rank of General Who Exerts Martial Force.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷度支尚書，領太子左率。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to Minister of the Treasury and oversaw the Left Leader of the Heir Apparent's guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was moved to Minister of the Treasury while continuing to oversee the Left Leader of the Heir Apparent's guard.

sentences.zh: 冬，虜主攻沔北五郡，假慧景節，率衆二萬，騎千匹，向襄陽。

translations.literal: In winter the barbarians' main force attacked the five commanderies north of the Han; Huijing was lent the staff to lead twenty thousand troops and a thousand horses toward Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter the barbarians' main army attacked the five commanderies north of the Han; Huijing was lent the staff to lead twenty thousand troops and a thousand horses toward Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 雍州衆軍竝受節度。

translations.literal: All the armies of Yong province were subject to his command.
translations.idiomatic: All the armies of Yong province were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，慧景至襄陽，五郡已沒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai Huijing reached Xiangyang; the five commanderies had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, Huijing reached Xiangyang, but the five commanderies had already been lost.

sentences.zh: 加慧景平北將軍，置佐史，分軍助戍樊城。

translations.literal: Huijing was given additional title General Who Pacifies the North, staff officers appointed, troops divided to aid in garrisoning Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North; staff officers were appointed and troops were detached to help garrison Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 慧景頓渦口村，與太子中庶子梁王及軍主前寧州刺史董仲民、劉山陽、裴颺、傅法憲等五千餘人進行鄧城。

translations.literal: Huijing halted at Wokou village and with Heir Apparent Attendant the Prince of Liang and army commanders the former Inspector of Ningzhou Dong Zhongmin, Liu Shanyang, Pei Yang, Fu Faxian, and more than five thousand men advanced toward Dengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing halted at Wokou village. With Heir Apparent Attendant the Prince of Liang and the army commanders—the former Inspector of Ningzhou Dong Zhongmin, Liu Shanyang, Pei Yang, and Fu Faxian—he advanced on Dengcheng with more than five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 前參騎還，稱虜軍且至。

translations.literal: Forward scouts returned reporting barbarian troops were about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Forward scouts came back reporting that barbarian troops were about to arrive.

sentences.zh: 須臾，望數萬騎俱來，慧景據南門，梁王據北門，令諸軍上城上。

translations.literal: Before long they saw tens of thousands of horsemen all coming; Huijing held the south gate, the Prince of Liang the north gate, and ordered all troops onto the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they saw tens of thousands of horsemen bearing down together; Huijing took the south gate, the Prince of Liang the north gate, and ordered all the troops up onto the walls.

sentences.zh: 時慧景等蓐食輕行，皆有饑懼之色。

translations.literal: At that time Huijing and the others had eaten a light meal and traveled lightly; all had the color of hunger and fear.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huijing and the others had eaten a light meal and marched with little baggage; everyone looked hungry and afraid.

sentences.zh: 軍中北館客三人，走投虜，具告之。

translations.literal: Three northern lodging guests in the army deserted to the barbarians and told them everything.
translations.idiomatic: Three northern lodging guests in the army deserted to the barbarians and told them the whole situation.

sentences.zh: 虜偽都督中軍大將軍彭城王元勰分遣偽武衞將軍元蚪趣城東南，斷慧景歸路，偽司馬孟斌向城東，偽右衞將軍播正屯城北，交射城內。

translations.literal: The barbarians' false commander, Central Army Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie, sent the false Martial Guard General Yuan Dou to hurry to the southeast of the city and cut Huijing's line of retreat; false Chief Clerk Meng Bin toward the east of the city; false General of the Right Wei Bo Zheng encamped north of the city—crossfire into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians' false commander, Central Army Grand General the Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie, sent the false Martial Guard General Yuan Dou to rush the southeast of the city and cut off Huijing's retreat; the false Chief Clerk Meng Bin toward the east of the city; and the false General of the Right Wei Bo Zheng to camp north of the city, all shooting into the town.

sentences.zh: 梁王欲出戰，慧景曰：「虜不夜圍人城，待日暮自當去也。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang wished to sally forth and fight; Huijing said: "Barbarians do not besiege cities at night; wait until evening and they will naturally go."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang wished to sally out and fight; Huijing said: "Barbarians do not lay siege to cities at night; wait until evening and they will leave of themselves."

sentences.zh: 旣而虜衆轉盛，慧景於南門拔軍，衆軍不相知，隨後奔退。

translations.literal: Soon after the barbarian force grew stronger; Huijing at the south gate withdrew the army; the other troops did not know and followed in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the barbarian host grew stronger; Huijing at the south gate pulled back his troops, but the other units did not know and fell back in flight behind him.

sentences.zh: 虜軍從北門入，劉山陽與部曲數百人斷後死戰，虜遣鎧馬百餘匹突取山陽，山陽使射手射之，三人倒馬，手殺十餘人，不能禁，且戰且退。

translations.literal: Barbarian troops entered from the north gate; Liu Shanyang with several hundred of his command fought a rear-guard action to the death; the barbarians sent more than a hundred armored horses to rush and seize Shanyang; Shanyang had archers shoot, three men and horses fell, he killed more than ten with his own hand yet could not stop them, fighting while retreating.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian troops entered from the north gate. Liu Shanyang with several hundred of his men fought a desperate rear-guard action; the barbarians sent more than a hundred armored horsemen to seize him. Shanyang had his archers shoot; three riders and horses went down, and he killed more than ten with his own hand, yet could not hold them back and fought as he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 慧景南出過鬧溝，軍人蹈藉，橋皆斷壞，虜軍夾路射之，軍主傅法憲見殺，赴溝死者相枕。

translations.literal: Huijing went south past Naogou; soldiers trampled one another, bridges all broke, barbarians shot from both sides of the road—army commander Fu Faxian was killed, those who fell into the ditch died in heaps one atop another.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing went south past Naogou; soldiers trampled one another, every bridge broke, and the barbarians shot from both sides of the road. The army commander Fu Faxian was killed; those who fell into the ditches died in heaps, bodies piled on bodies.

sentences.zh: 山陽取襖杖填溝，乘之得免。

translations.literal: Shanyang took padded coats and staffs, filled the ditch, and crossed to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang took padded coats and staffs, stuffed the ditch full, and crossed over to escape.

sentences.zh: 虜主率大衆追之，晡時，虜主至沔北，圍軍主劉山陽。

translations.literal: The barbarian lord led the main host in pursuit; in the late afternoon the barbarian lord reached north of the Han and surrounded army commander Liu Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian lord led the main host in pursuit; in the late afternoon he reached the north bank of the Han and surrounded the army commander Liu Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 山陽據城苦戰，至暮，虜乃退。

translations.literal: Shanyang held the city and fought bitterly; by evening the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang held the city and fought desperately; by nightfall the barbarians at last withdrew.

sentences.zh: 衆軍恐懼，其夕皆下船還襄陽。

translations.literal: All the armies were afraid; that evening they all went aboard ship and returned to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army was terrified; that same evening everyone went aboard ship and returned to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 明年，裴叔業以壽春降虜，改授慧景平西將軍，假節、侍中、護軍如故，率軍水路征壽陽。

translations.literal: The next year Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the barbarians; Huijing was reassigned as General Who Pacifies the West, lent the staff, Palace Attendant, and Protecting Army as before, and led troops by river to campaign against Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the barbarians. Huijing was reassigned General Who Pacifies the West, retaining his lent staff, Palace Attendant post, and Protecting Army command, and led troops by water against Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 軍頓白下，將發，帝長圍屏除出琅邪城送之。

translations.literal: The army halted at Baixia; about to set out, the emperor removed the long encircling screens and came out from Langya city to see them off.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Baixia. As they were about to depart, the emperor had the long encircling screens removed and came out from Langya city to escort them.

sentences.zh: 帝戎服坐城樓上，召慧景單騎進圍內，無一人自隨者。

translations.literal: The emperor in military dress sat on the city tower, summoned Huijing to enter the encirclement alone on horseback—no one followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in military dress, sat on the city tower and summoned Huijing to ride in alone—without a single attendant.

sentences.zh: 裁交數言，拜辭而去。

translations.literal: They exchanged only a few words; he bowed in farewell and left.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged only a few words; he bowed in farewell and departed.

sentences.zh: 慧景旣得出，甚喜。

translations.literal: Once Huijing had gotten out he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huijing was outside the encirclement he was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 子覺爲直閤將軍，慧景密與期：四月慧景至廣陵，覺便出奔。

translations.literal: His son Jue was Direct Attendant General; Huijing secretly agreed with him: when Huijing reached Guangling in the fourth month, Jue would flee and join him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jue was Direct Attendant General. Huijing secretly arranged with him that when Huijing reached Guangling in the fourth month, Jue would flee the capital to join him.

sentences.zh: 慧景過廣陵數十里，召會諸軍主曰：「吾荷三帝厚恩，當顧託之重。

translations.literal: When Huijing had passed Guangling by several tens of li he summoned the army commanders and said: "I have received thick favor from three emperors and bear the weight of their dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Huijing had passed Guangling by several dozen li he summoned the army commanders and said: "I have received deep grace from three emperors and bear the weight of their deathbed trust.

sentences.zh: 幼主昏狂，朝廷壞亂，危而不扶，責在今日。

translations.literal: The young emperor is muddled and mad, the court is ruined and in chaos; to see danger and not support it—the blame lies with us today.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor is muddled and deranged, the court is broken and in chaos. To see peril and not steady it—the duty falls on us today.

sentences.zh: 欲與諸君共建大功，以安宗社，何如？」

translations.literal: I wish to join you all in establishing a great achievement to settle the altars of state—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to join you in achieving a great deed and securing the altars of state. What say you?"

sentences.zh: 衆皆響應。

translations.literal: All responded in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: All answered with a shout of assent.

sentences.zh: 於是回軍還廣陵，司馬崔恭祖守廣陵城，開門納之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he turned the army back to Guangling; Chief Clerk Cui Gongzu held Guangling city and opened the gates to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he turned the army back to Guangling. His Chief Clerk Cui Gongzu held Guangling city and opened the gates to receive them.

sentences.zh: 帝聞變，以征虜將軍右衞將軍左興盛假節，督京邑水陸衆軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of the revolt he made Conquering Barbarians General and General of the Right Wei Zuo Xingsheng lent the staff to command the capital land and water forces.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of the uprising he appointed Conquering Barbarians General and General of the Right Wei Zuo Xingsheng, lent the staff, to command the capital's land and water armies.

sentences.zh: 慧景停二日，便收衆濟江集京口。

translations.literal: Huijing halted two days, then gathered the host and crossed the river to assemble at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing halted two days, then gathered his forces, crossed the river, and assembled at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 江夏王寶玄又爲內應，合二鎮兵力，奉寶玄向京師。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia Bao Xuan also acted as inner ally; combining the strength of the two garrisons they supported Bao Xuan toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jiangxia, Bao Xuan, also served as an inside collaborator; joining the strength of the two commanderies they marched Bao Xuan toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 臺遣驍騎將軍張佛護、直閤將軍徐元稱、屯騎校尉姚景珍、西中郎參軍徐景智、游盪軍主董伯珍、騎官桓靈福等據竹里爲數城。

translations.literal: The court sent Valiant Cavalry General Zhang Fuhu, Direct Attendant General Xu Yuancheng, Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Yao Jingzhen, Western Palace Adviser Xu Jingzhi, Roaming Army Commander Dong Bozhen, Cavalry Officer Huan Lingfu, and others to hold Zhuli in several forts.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Valiant Cavalry General Zhang Fuhu, Direct Attendant General Xu Yuancheng, Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Yao Jingzhen, Western Palace Adviser Xu Jingzhi, Roaming Army Commander Dong Bozhen, Cavalry Officer Huan Lingfu, and others to hold Zhuli in a chain of forts.

sentences.zh: 寶玄遣信謂佛護曰：「身自還朝，君何意苦相斷遏？」

translations.literal: Bao Xuan sent a message to Fuhu saying: "I myself am returning to court—why do you insist on cutting me off so bitterly?"
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan sent word to Fuhu: "I am returning to court myself—why do you mean to block me so harshly?"

sentences.zh: 佛護答曰：「小人荷國重恩，使於此創立小戍。

translations.literal: Fuhu answered: "This petty man bears the state's heavy grace and was sent to establish this little garrison here.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhu answered: "I, a humble servant, bear the state's heavy grace and was sent to raise this small garrison.

sentences.zh: 殿下還朝，但自直過，豈敢干斷。」

translations.literal: When Your Highness returns to court, simply pass straight through—how would I dare interfere?"
translations.idiomatic: When Your Highness returns to court, pass straight through—that is all I ask. How would I dare obstruct you?"

sentences.zh: 遂射慧景軍，因合戰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he shot at Huijing's army and battle was joined.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he shot at Huijing's army and battle was joined.

sentences.zh: 慧景子覺及崔恭祖領前鋒，皆傖楚善戰；

translations.literal: Huijing's son Jue and Cui Gongzu led the vanguard—both were northern braves skilled in battle;
translations.idiomatic: Huijing's son Jue and Cui Gongzu led the vanguard—northern braves, skilled fighters both;

sentences.zh: 又輕行不爨食，以數舫緣江載酒肉爲軍糧。

translations.literal: they also marched lightly without cooking food, using several boats along the river to carry wine and meat as army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: they also marched light without cooking, loading wine and meat on several boats along the river as army rations.

sentences.zh: 每見臺軍城中煙火起，輙盡力攻擊，臺軍不復得食，以此饑困。

translations.literal: Whenever they saw smoke rise from cooking fires in the court army's forts they pressed the attack with all their strength; the court troops could no longer eat and were worn down by hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they saw smoke rise from the court army's forts they attacked with full force; the court troops could no longer cook and were worn down by hunger.

sentences.zh: 元稱等議欲降，佛護不許。

translations.literal: Yuancheng and others wished to surrender but Fuhu would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuancheng and others wanted to surrender, but Fuhu would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 十二日，恭祖等復攻之，城陷，佛護單馬走，追得斬首，徐元稱降，餘軍主皆死。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day Gongzu and others attacked again; the fort fell. Fuhu fled alone on horseback, was pursued and beheaded; Xu Yuancheng surrendered; the remaining commanders all died.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day Gongzu and the others attacked again and the fort fell. Fuhu fled alone on horseback, was pursued and beheaded. Xu Yuancheng surrendered; the remaining commanders were all killed.

sentences.zh: 慧景至臨沂，令李玉之發橋斷路，慧景收殺之。

translations.literal: Huijing reached Linyi and ordered Li Yuzhi to raise the bridge and cut the road; Huijing seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huijing reached Linyi he ordered Li Yuzhi to raise the bridge and cut the road; Huijing seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 臺遣中領軍王瑩都督衆軍，據湖頭築壘，上帶蔣山西巖，實甲數萬。

translations.literal: The court sent Central Palace Leader Wang Ying to command the armies, holding Hutou and building ramparts, above on the western cliff of Mount Jiang, with armor in the tens of thousands in truth.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Central Palace Leader Wang Ying to command the armies, holding Hutou and building ramparts along the western cliff of Mount Jiang, with tens of thousands of armored men in position.

sentences.zh: 慧景至查硎，竹塘人萬副兒善射獵，能捕虎，投慧景曰：「今平路皆爲臺軍所斷，不可議進。

translations.literal: Huijing reached Chayao; Wan Fuer of Zhutang, skilled in shooting and hunting, able to catch tigers, came to Huijing and said: "Now the level roads are all cut by the court army—we cannot discuss advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing reached Chayao. Wan Fuer of Zhutang, skilled in the hunt and able to take tigers, came to him and said: "The level roads are all held by the court army—we cannot think of advancing directly.

sentences.zh: 唯宜從蔣山龍尾上，出其不意耳。」

translations.literal: Only by taking the Dragon Tail path up Mount Jiang and coming out where they do not expect us."
translations.idiomatic: We should take the Dragon Tail path up Mount Jiang and strike where they do not expect us."

sentences.zh: 慧景從之，分遣千餘人魚貫緣山，自西巖夜下，鼓呌臨城中。

translations.literal: Huijing followed this; he sent more than a thousand men in single file along the mountain, coming down from the western cliff by night, beating drums and shouting at the city below.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing followed his advice, sending more than a thousand men in single file along the mountain, descending from the western cliff by night, beating drums and shouting at the city below.

sentences.zh: 臺軍驚恐，卽時奔散。

translations.literal: The court army was terrified and at once scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The court army was terrified and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣右衞將軍左興盛率臺內三萬人，拒慧景於北籬門，望風退走。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent General of the Right Wei Zuo Xingsheng with thirty thousand men from within the palace to resist Huijing at the northern fence gate; they saw the wind and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent General of the Right Wei Zuo Xingsheng with thirty thousand palace troops to resist Huijing at the northern fence gate; they saw his strength and fled.

sentences.zh: 慧景引軍入樂遊苑，恭祖率輕騎十餘匹突進北掖門，乃復出，宮門皆閉。

translations.literal: Huijing led the army into the Leyou Park; Gongzu with more than ten light horsemen burst through the northern side gate and came out again—the palace gates were all shut.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing led his army into the Leyou Park. Gongzu with a dozen light horsemen charged through the northern side gate and came out again; every palace gate was shut.

sentences.zh: 慧景引衆圍之。

translations.literal: Huijing led the host to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing led the host to besiege the palace.

sentences.zh: 於是東府、石頭、白下、新亭諸城皆潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Eastern Palace, Stone Fortress, Baixia, Xinting, and the other forts all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Eastern Palace, Stone Fortress, Baixia, Xinting, and the other strongpoints all fell.

sentences.zh: 左興盛走，不得入宮，逃淮渚荻舫中，慧景擒殺之。

translations.literal: Zuo Xingsheng fled, could not enter the palace, and escaped to a reed boat on the Huai; Huijing seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Xingsheng fled, could not enter the palace, and hid in a reed boat on the Huai; Huijing captured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 宮中遣兵出盪，不剋。

translations.literal: The palace sent troops out to strike but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The palace sent troops out to attack but could not overcome them.

sentences.zh: 慧景燒蘭臺府署爲戰場，守衞尉蕭暢屯南掖門處分城內，隨方應擊，衆心以此稍安。

translations.literal: Huijing burned the Orchid Terrace offices as a battlefield; Defender of the Palace Wei Xiao Chang held the southern side gate and directed the city's defense, responding to attacks as they came; popular sentiment grew somewhat calmer on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing burned the Orchid Terrace offices for a battlefield. Defender of the Palace Wei Xiao Chang held the southern side gate and directed the city's defense, meeting attacks wherever they came; on this account popular sentiment grew somewhat calmer.

sentences.zh: 慧景稱宣德太后令，廢帝爲吳王。

translations.literal: Huijing proclaimed an order in the name of Dowager Empress Xuande deposing the emperor as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing proclaimed an order in the name of Dowager Empress Xuande, deposing the emperor as Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 時巴陵王昭冑先逃民間，出投慧景，慧景意更向之，故猶豫未知所立。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Baling Zhaozhou had fled first among the people and came to join Huijing; Huijing's inclination turned more toward him, so he hesitated, not knowing whom to establish.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Baling, Zhaozhou, had fled among the people and came to join Huijing. Huijing's mind turned more toward him, so he hesitated, not knowing whom to enthrone.

sentences.zh: 竹里之捷，子覺與恭祖爭勳，慧景不能決。

translations.literal: After the victory at Zhuli, son Jue and Gongzu contended over merit; Huijing could not decide between them.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Zhuli, Jue and Gongzu quarreled over credit; Huijing could not settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 恭祖勸慧景射火箭燒北掖樓，慧景以大事垂定，後若更造，費用功力，不從其計。

translations.literal: Gongzu urged Huijing to shoot fire arrows and burn the northern side tower; Huijing, since the great affair was nearly settled and rebuilding afterward would cost labor, did not follow this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu urged Huijing to shoot fire arrows and burn the northern side tower. Huijing, thinking the great affair was nearly settled and that rebuilding would cost effort afterward, would not follow this plan.

sentences.zh: 性好談義，兼解佛理，頓法輪寺，對客高談。

translations.literal: He loved to discuss doctrine and also understood Buddhist principles; he halted at Falun Temple and held lofty discourse with guests.
translations.idiomatic: He loved disputation and also understood Buddhist teaching; he halted at Falun Temple and held lofty discourse with his guests.

sentences.zh: 恭祖深懷怨望。

translations.literal: Gongzu harbored deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu nursed deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 先是衞尉蕭懿爲征虜將軍、豫州刺史，自歷陽步道征壽陽。

translations.literal: Earlier Defender of the Palace Xiao Yi had been Conquering Barbarians General and Inspector of Yuzhou and was campaigning against Shouchun by the Liyang foot route.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Defender of the Palace Xiao Yi had been Conquering Barbarians General and Inspector of Yuzhou and was marching against Shouchun by the Liyang foot route.

sentences.zh: 帝遣密使告之，懿率軍主胡松、李居士等數千人自采石濟岸，頓越城，舉火，臺城中鼓呌稱慶。

translations.literal: The emperor sent secret envoys to inform him; Yi led army commanders Hu Song, Li Jushi, and several thousand men across from Caishi, halted at Yuecheng, raised beacon fires, and within the capital walls drums and shouts proclaimed celebration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent secret envoys to inform him. Yi led the army commanders Hu Song, Li Jushi, and several thousand men across from Caishi, halted at Yuecheng, raised beacon fires, and within the capital drums and shouts of celebration rang out.

sentences.zh: 恭祖先勸慧景遣二千人斷西岸軍，令不得渡，慧景以城旦夕降，外救自然應散。

translations.literal: Gongzu had first urged Huijing to send two thousand men to cut off the army on the western bank and not let them cross; Huijing thought the city would surrender within days and outside aid would naturally scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu had first urged Huijing to send two thousand men to cut off the army on the western bank and keep them from crossing. Huijing thought the city would fall within days and outside relief would scatter of itself.

sentences.zh: 至是恭祖請擊義師，又不許。

translations.literal: Now Gongzu asked to strike the army of righteousness but again was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Now Gongzu asked to strike the loyalist army but again was refused.

sentences.zh: 乃遣子覺將精手數千人渡南岸。

translations.literal: He sent son Jue with several thousand picked men to cross the southern bank.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Jue with several thousand picked men to cross the southern bank.

sentences.zh: 義師昧旦進戰，數合，士皆致死，覺大敗，赴淮死者二千餘人，覺單馬退，開桁阻淮。

translations.literal: The army of righteousness fought at dawn; after several engagements the men all fought to the death. Jue was utterly defeated; more than two thousand who fell into the Huai drowned; Jue fled alone on horseback, raised the bridge, and blocked the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalist army fought at dawn. After several clashes the men fought to the death. Jue was utterly defeated; more than two thousand who fell into the Huai drowned. Jue fled alone on horseback, raised the bridge, and blocked the crossing.

sentences.zh: 其夜，崔恭祖與驍將劉靈運詣城降，慧景衆情離壞，乃將腹心數人潛去，欲北渡江，城北諸軍不知，猶爲拒戰。

translations.literal: That night Cui Gongzu and the valiant general Liu Lingyun came to the city to surrender; Huijing's host's will broke apart. He took several trusted men and slipped away, intending to cross the river north; the armies north of the city did not know and still fought in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: That night Cui Gongzu and the valiant general Liu Lingyun came to the city to surrender. Huijing's army fell apart in spirit. He took a few trusted men and slipped away, intending to cross the river north; the armies north of the city did not know and still fought on.

sentences.zh: 城內出盪，殺數百人。

translations.literal: Troops sallied from within the city and killed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Troops sallied from the city and killed several hundred.

sentences.zh: 義軍渡北岸，慧景餘衆皆奔。

translations.literal: The army of righteousness crossed the northern bank; Huijing's remaining host all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalist army crossed to the northern bank; Huijing's remaining troops all fled.

sentences.zh: 慧景圍城凡十二日，軍旅散在京師，不爲營壘。

translations.literal: Huijing besieged the city altogether twelve days; the army and travelers scattered through the capital without building camps.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing had besieged the city twelve days in all; his troops and camp followers scattered through the capital without building proper camps.

sentences.zh: 及走，衆於道稍散，單馬至蟹浦，爲漁父所斬，以頭內魚籃，檐送至京師，時年六十三。

translations.literal: When he fled the host gradually dispersed along the road; alone on horseback he reached Xiepu and was beheaded by a fisherman, his head placed in a fish basket and carried on a pole to the capital—he was sixty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: When he fled his followers gradually scattered along the road. Alone on horseback he reached Xiepu, where a fisherman beheaded him, put his head in a fish basket, and carried it on a pole to the capital. He was sixty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 追贈張佛護爲司州刺史，左興盛豫州刺史，竝征虜將軍，徐景智桓靈福屯騎校尉，董伯珍員外郎，李玉之給事中，其餘有差。

translations.literal: Posthumously Zhang Fuhu was honored as Inspector of Si province, Zuo Xingsheng as Inspector of Yu province—both Conquering Barbarians Generals; Xu Jingzhi and Huan Lingfu as Colonels of the Garrison Cavalry; Dong Bozhen as Outer Gentleman; Li Yuzhi as Recipient for the Palace; the rest with differing ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuhu was posthumously honored as Inspector of Si province; Zuo Xingsheng as Inspector of Yu province—both as Conquering Barbarians Generals; Xu Jingzhi and Huan Lingfu as Colonels of the Garrison Cavalry; Dong Bozhen as Outer Gentleman; Li Yuzhi as Recipient for the Palace; the rest with differing honors.

sentences.zh: 恭祖者，慧景宗人，驍果便馬槊，氣力絕人，頻經軍陣。

translations.literal: Gongzu was Huijing's clansman, fierce and skilled with the cavalry lance, with strength beyond ordinary men, having passed through many battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu was Huijing's clansman—fierce, skilled with the cavalry lance, with strength beyond ordinary men, having seen many battle lines.

sentences.zh: 討王敬則，與左興盛軍容袁文曠爭敬則首，訴明帝曰：「恭祖禿馬絳衫，手刺倒賊。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Wang Jingze he and Zuo Xingsheng's army aide Yuan Wenkuan contended over Jingze's head, appealing to Emperor Ming: "Gongzu in a bald head and crimson shirt personally stabbed and felled the bandit.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Wang Jingze he and Zuo Xingsheng's army aide Yuan Wenkuan fought over Jingze's head, telling Emperor Ming: "Gongzu, bald-headed in a crimson shirt, personally stabbed and felled the rebel.

sentences.zh: 故文曠得斬其首。

translations.literal: Therefore Wenkuan was able to cut off his head.
translations.idiomatic: So Wenkuan was able to cut off the head.

sentences.zh: 以死易勳，而見枉奪。

translations.literal: To trade death for merit yet be wrongly deprived of it.
translations.idiomatic: To risk death for merit yet be wrongly stripped of it.

sentences.zh: 若失此勳，要當刺殺左興盛。」

translations.literal: If I lose this merit I shall surely stab and kill Zuo Xingsheng."
translations.idiomatic: If I lose this merit I mean to stab Zuo Xingsheng to death."

sentences.zh: 帝以其勇，使謂興盛曰：「何容令恭祖與文曠爭功。」

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his courage, had someone tell Xingsheng: "How can you let Gongzu and Wenkuan contend over merit?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, impressed by his ferocity, had someone tell Xingsheng: "How can you let Gongzu and Wenkuan fight over the credit?"

sentences.zh: 遂封二百戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was enfeoffed with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was enfeoffed with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 慧景平後，恭祖繫尚方，少時殺之。

translations.literal: After Huijing was pacified, Gongzu was imprisoned in the Palace Workshops and soon after executed.
translations.idiomatic: After Huijing's revolt was suppressed, Gongzu was imprisoned in the Palace Workshops and soon executed.

sentences.zh: 覺亡命爲道人，見執伏法。

translations.literal: Jue fled and became a monk; he was seized and executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Jue fled and became a monk; he was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 臨刑與妹書曰：「捨逆旅，歸其家，以爲大樂；

translations.literal: Facing execution he wrote his sister: "To leave a traveler's lodge and return home is deemed the greatest joy;
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of execution he wrote his sister: "To leave a traveler's lodge and return home is held the greatest joy;

sentences.zh: 況得從先君遊太清乎。

translations.literal: how much more to follow one's late father in roaming the Great Clarity?
translations.idiomatic: how much more to follow one's late father in roaming the Great Clarity?

sentences.zh: 古人有力扛周鼎，而有立錐之歎，以此言死，亦復何傷！

translations.literal: Men of old had strength to shoulder the Zhou tripod yet sighed over having no space to set a awl—speaking of death thus, what injury is there!
translations.idiomatic: Men of old had strength to shoulder the Zhou tripod yet sighed that they had not room to stand an awl—speaking of death in this way, what harm is there!

sentences.zh: 平生素心，士大夫皆知之矣。

translations.literal: My lifelong plain heart is known to gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: My plain heart through life is known to gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 旣不得附驥尾，安得施名於後世，慕古竹帛之事，今皆亡矣。」

translations.literal: Having failed to attach to a steed's tail, how could I leave a name to posterity? The old affairs of bamboo and silk are now all gone."
translations.idiomatic: Having failed to attach to a steed's tail, how could I leave a name to posterity? The old affairs recorded on bamboo and silk are now all gone."

sentences.zh: 慧景妻女亦頗知佛義。

translations.literal: Huijing's wife and daughters also understood Buddhist principles rather well.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing's wife and daughters also understood Buddhist teaching rather well.

sentences.zh: 覺弟偃，爲始安內史，藏竄得免。

translations.literal: Jue's younger brother Yan was Interior Minister of Shian and hid in concealment, escaping punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Jue's younger brother Yan was Interior Minister of Shian; he hid and escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 和帝西臺立，以爲寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: When the Western Terrace of the Emperor He was established he was made General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Terrace of the Emperor He was established, Yan was made General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，詣公車門上書曰：

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing he went to the Imperial Coach Gate and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing he went to the Imperial Coach Gate and submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟太祖、高宗之孝子忠臣，而昏主之賊臣亂子者，江夏王與陛下，先臣與鎮軍是也。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that the filial loyal ministers of the Founding Emperor and Emperor Ming are, among the wicked ministers and rebellious sons of a muddled ruler, the Prince of Jiangxia and Your Majesty on one side, and my late father and the Commander on the other.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects that among the filial loyal ministers of the Founding Emperor and Emperor Ming, set against the wicked ministers and rebellious sons of a muddled ruler, stand the Prince of Jiangxia and Your Majesty on one side, and my late father and the Commander on the other.

sentences.zh: 臣聞堯舜之心，常以天下爲憂，而不以位爲樂。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the hearts of Yao and Shun always took the realm as their worry and not position as their joy.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that the hearts of Yao and Shun always took the realm as their worry and not the throne as their joy.

sentences.zh: 彼孑然之舜，壟畝之人，猶尚若此；

translations.literal: That solitary Shun, a man of the fields, still felt thus;
translations.idiomatic: That solitary Shun, a man of the fields, still felt thus;

sentences.zh: 況祖業之重，家國之切？

translations.literal: how much more the weight of ancestral enterprise and the urgency of state and family?
translations.idiomatic: how much more the weight of ancestral enterprise and the urgency of state and family?

sentences.zh: 江夏旣行之於前，陛下又蹈之於後，雖成敗異術，而所由同方也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia already acted thus before; Your Majesty now treads the same path afterward—though success and failure differ in method, the road taken is the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jiangxia already acted thus before; Your Majesty now treads the same path afterward. Though success and failure differ in method, the road taken is the same.

sentences.zh: 陛下初登至尊，與天合符。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly ascended to supreme honor and matches Heaven in your mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has newly ascended to supreme honor and matches Heaven in your mandate.

sentences.zh: 天下纖介之屈，尚望陛下申之，絲髮之冤，尚望陛下理之。

translations.literal: A wrong as fine as a fiber in the realm still hopes Your Majesty will redress it; an injustice as thin as a hair still hopes Your Majesty will set it right.
translations.idiomatic: A wrong as fine as a fiber in the realm still hopes Your Majesty will redress it; an injustice as thin as a hair still hopes Your Majesty will set it right.

sentences.zh: 況先帝之子，陛下之兄，所行之道，卽陛下所由哉？

translations.literal: How much more a son of the late emperor, Your Majesty's elder brother—the path he walked is the very path Your Majesty has taken?
translations.idiomatic: How much more a son of the late emperor, Your Majesty's elder brother—the path he walked is the very path Your Majesty has taken?

sentences.zh: 如此尚弗恤，其餘何幾哉？

translations.literal: If even this is not pitied, what else remains?
translations.idiomatic: If even this is not pitied, what else remains?

sentences.zh: 陛下德侔造化，仁育羣生，雖在昆蟲草木，有不得其所者，覽而傷焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's virtue matches transforming creation; your kindness nurtures the masses—even among insects and plants, if any lack their proper place you look on them with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue matches transforming creation; your kindness nurtures the masses—even among insects and plants, if any lack their proper place you look on them with grief.

sentences.zh: 而況乎友愛天至，孔懷之深。

translations.literal: How much more the Heaven-sent depth of brotherly love and the intimacy of flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: How much more the Heaven-sent depth of brotherly love and the intimacy of flesh and bone.

sentences.zh: 夫豈不懷，將以事割。

translations.literal: Could one not cherish it? Yet affairs must be cut off for the sake of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Could one not cherish it? Yet affairs must be cut off for the sake of the state.

sentences.zh: 此實左右不明，未之或詳。

translations.literal: This is truly that those at your side do not make it clear and have not examined it in detail.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly that those at your side do not make it clear and have not examined it in detail.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下公聽竝觀，以詢之芻蕘。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty listens publicly and views together, and inquires even of the grass and firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty listens publicly and views together, and inquires even of the grass and firewood.

sentences.zh: 羣臣有以臣言爲不可，乞使臣廷辯之。

translations.literal: If any minister holds your servant's words impossible, I beg to debate it before the court.
translations.idiomatic: If any minister holds your servant's words impossible, I beg to debate it before the court.

sentences.zh: 則天人之意塞，四海之疑釋。

translations.literal: Then the intent of Heaven and man will be settled and the doubts of the four seas dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Then the intent of Heaven and man will be settled and the doubts of the four seas dissolved.

sentences.zh: 必若不然，僥小民之無識耳。

translations.literal: If it must not be so, it is only that petty people lack understanding.
translations.idiomatic: If it must not be so, it is only that petty people lack understanding.

sentences.zh: 使其曉然知此，相聚而逃，陛下以責江夏之冤，朝廷將何以應之哉？

translations.literal: If they clearly know this they will gather and flee; Your Majesty will blame the Prince of Jiangxia's wrong—how will the court answer?
translations.idiomatic: If they clearly know this they will gather and flee; Your Majesty will blame the Prince of Jiangxia's wrong—how will the court answer?

sentences.zh: 若天聽沛然回光，發惻愴之詔，而使東牟朱虛東褒儀父之節，則何戈之士，誰不盡死？

translations.literal: If Heaven's hearing is suddenly moved to turn its light and a compassionate edict is issued, granting the integrity of Dongmou, Zhu Xu, Dongxiang, and Yifu—then what soldier bearing a spear would not die to the last man?
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's hearing is suddenly moved to turn its light and a compassionate edict is issued, granting the integrity of Dongmou, Zhu Xu, Dongxiang, and Yifu—then what soldier bearing a spear would not die to the last man?

sentences.zh: 愚戇之言，萬一上合，事乞留中。

translations.literal: This foolish loyal speech—if by the slightest chance it accords with Your Majesty, I beg the matter be kept within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: This foolish loyal speech—if by the slightest chance it accords with Your Majesty, I beg the matter be kept within the palace.

sentences.zh: 事寢不報。

translations.literal: The affair was shelved without response.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 偃又上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yan again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yan again submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 近冒陳江夏之冤，定承聖詔，已有褒贈，此臣狂疏之罪也。

translations.literal: Recently I rashly stated the Prince of Jiangxia's wrong; I assumed a sacred edict had already granted posthumous honor—this is your servant's rash memorial's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I rashly stated the Prince of Jiangxia's wrong; I assumed a sacred edict had already granted posthumous honor—this is your servant's rash memorial's crime.

sentences.zh: 然臣所以諮問者，不得其實，罪在萬沒，無所復云。

translations.literal: Yet the reason your servant inquired was that he did not obtain the truth; the crime merits ten thousand deaths and there is nothing more to say.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the reason your servant inquired was that he did not obtain the truth; the crime merits ten thousand deaths and there is nothing more to say.

sentences.zh: 但愚心所恨，非敢以父子之親，骨肉之閒，而僥幸曲陛下之法，傷至公之義。

translations.literal: But what your servant's foolish heart resents is not daring, because of father-son kinship and flesh-and-bone closeness, to bend Your Majesty's law by chance and wound the utmost public righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: But what your servant's foolish heart resents is not daring, because of father-son kinship and flesh-and-bone closeness, to bend Your Majesty's law by chance and wound the utmost public righteousness.

sentences.zh: 誠不曉聖朝所以然之意。

translations.literal: Your servant truly does not understand the meaning of the holy court's action.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant truly does not understand what the holy court intends by this.

sentences.zh: 若以狂主雖狂，而實是天子，江夏雖賢，實是人臣，先臣奉人臣逆人君，以爲不可申明詔，得矣；

translations.literal: If because the mad ruler though mad is in truth the Son of Heaven, and the Prince of Jiangxia though worthy is in truth a subject—my late father as subject opposing his ruler could not proclaim the edict, that would be acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: If one says that though the mad ruler is mad he is truly Son of Heaven, and though the Prince of Jiangxia is worthy he is truly a subject—then my late father as subject opposing his ruler could not have proclaimed the edict, and that would be acceptable;

sentences.zh: 然未審陛下亦是人臣不？

translations.literal: yet your servant does not examine whether Your Majesty is also a subject or not?
translations.idiomatic: yet has Your Majesty examined whether you yourself are also a subject?

sentences.zh: 而鎮軍亦復奉人臣逆人君，今之嚴兵勁卒，方指於象魏者，其故何哉？

translations.literal: And the Commander again as subject opposes his ruler—now the stern troops and keen soldiers are pointing at the Gate of Bright Law—for what reason?
translations.idiomatic: And the Commander again as subject opposes his ruler—now stern troops and keen soldiers are pointing at the Gate of Bright Law—for what reason?

sentences.zh: 臣所不死，苟存視息，非有他故，所以待皇運之開泰，申冤魂之枉屈。

translations.literal: What your servant does not die for, clinging to breath and sight, has no other cause: to await the opening and peace of the imperial fortune and to declare the wronged souls' injustice.
translations.idiomatic: What keeps your servant alive, clinging to breath and sight, has no other cause: to await the opening of imperial fortune and to declare the injustice done to wronged souls.

sentences.zh: 今皇運旣已開泰矣，而死於社稷盡忠，反以爲賊，臣何用此生陛下世矣。

translations.literal: Now imperial fortune has already opened and reached peace, yet dying for the altars in full loyalty is instead deemed rebellion—of what use is this life to Your Majesty's age?
translations.idiomatic: Now imperial fortune has opened to peace, yet to die for the altars in full loyalty is called rebellion—of what use is this life in Your Majesty's age?

sentences.zh: 臣聞王臣之節，竭智盡公，以奉其上。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the integrity of a king's minister is to exhaust wisdom and give all to the public to serve his superior.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that a king's minister exhausts wisdom and gives all to the public to serve his superior.

sentences.zh: 居股肱之任者，申理冤滯，薦達羣賢。

translations.literal: Those who bear the duties of arm and thigh should straighten out wrongs held back, recommend and advance the worthy multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Those who bear the duties of arm and thigh should straighten out detained wrongs and recommend the worthy multitude.

sentences.zh: 凡此衆臣，夙興夜寐，心未嘗須臾之閒而不在公。

translations.literal: All these ministers rise early and sleep late; their hearts have not a moment's interval not upon the public.
translations.idiomatic: All these ministers rise early and sleep late; their hearts have not a moment's interval away from the public good.

sentences.zh: 故萬物無不得其理，而頌聲作焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the ten thousand things each obtain their principle and songs of praise arise.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the ten thousand things each obtain their principle and songs of praise arise.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案鎮軍將軍臣穎冑，宗室之親，股肱之重，身有伊、霍之功，荷陛下稷、旦之任。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes the Commander General Xiao Yingchao, kin of the imperial clan, weight of arm and thigh, himself having the merit of Yi and Huo, bearing Your Majesty's charge equal to Ji and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully notes Commander General Xiao Yingchao, kin of the imperial clan, pillar of the state, himself with the merit of Yi and Huo, bearing Your Majesty's charge equal to Ji and Dan.

sentences.zh: 中領軍臣詳，受帷幄之寄，副宰相之尊。

translations.literal: Central Palace Leader Xiang, receiving the court's inner trust, deputy to the prime minister's honor.
translations.idiomatic: Central Palace Leader Xiang, receiving the court's inner trust, deputy to the prime minister's honor.

sentences.zh: 皆所以棟樑朝廷，社稷之臣，天下所當，遑遑匪懈，盡忠竭誠，欲使萬物得理，而頌聲大興者，豈復宜踰此哉？

translations.literal: Both are beams and pillars of the court, ministers of the altars, what the realm looks to—how could they not be urgent and untiring, giving full loyalty and utmost sincerity, wishing the ten thousand things to obtain principle and great praise to arise—yet go beyond this?
translations.idiomatic: Both are beams and pillars of the court, ministers of the altars, what the realm looks to—how could they not be urgent and untiring, giving full loyalty, wishing the ten thousand things to obtain principle and great praise to arise—yet go beyond this?

sentences.zh: 而同知先臣股肱江夏，匡濟王室，天命未遂，王亡與亡，而不爲陛下瞥然一言。

translations.literal: Yet together they knew my late father as arm and thigh of Jiangxia, shoring up and saving the imperial house; Heaven's mandate was not fulfilled, the prince died and they died with him—yet they would not speak a single glance for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet together they knew my late father as Jiangxia's arm and thigh, shoring up the imperial house; Heaven's mandate was not fulfilled, the prince died and they died with him—yet they would not speak a single word for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 知而不言，是不忠之臣，不知而言，乃不智之臣，此而不知，將何所知？

translations.literal: To know and not speak is the disloyal minister; to speak without knowing is the unwise minister—this they do not know: what do they know?
translations.idiomatic: To know and not speak is a disloyal minister; to speak without knowing is an unwise minister—this they do not know: what do they know?

sentences.zh: 如以江夏心異先臣，受制臣力，則江夏同致死斃，聽可昏政淫刑，見殘無道。

translations.literal: If because the Prince of Jiangxia's mind differed from my late father and was constrained by my late father's force, then Jiangxia together reached death and ruin, listening to a muddled government with licentious punishments, being destroyed without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: If because the Prince of Jiangxia's mind differed from my late father and was constrained by my late father's force, then Jiangxia together reached death and ruin, enduring a muddled government with licentious punishments, destroyed without the Way.

sentences.zh: 然江夏之異，以何爲明，孔、呂二人，誰以爲戮。

translations.literal: Yet wherein was Jiangxia's difference clear—Kong and Lü, which was deemed for execution?
translations.idiomatic: Yet wherein was Jiangxia's difference clear—Kong and Lü, which was deemed for execution?

sentences.zh: 手御麾幡，言輙任公，同心共志，心若膠漆，而以爲異，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Hand on the command banner, words always trusting the public, hearts like glued lacquer—and yet this is called difference; your servant is privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Hand on the command banner, words always trusting the public, hearts like glued lacquer—and yet this is called difference; your servant is privately perplexed.

sentences.zh: 如以先臣遣使，江夏斬之，則征東之驛，何爲見戮？

translations.literal: If because my late father sent envoys and Jiangxia executed them—then why were the Eastern Campaign couriers killed?
translations.idiomatic: If because my late father sent envoys and Jiangxia executed them—then why were the Eastern Campaign couriers killed?

sentences.zh: 陛下斬征東之使，寔詐山陽；

translations.literal: Your Majesty executed the Eastern Campaign envoys, truly to deceive Shanyang;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty executed the Eastern Campaign envoys, truly to deceive Shanyang;

sentences.zh: 江夏違先臣之請，實謀孔矜。

translations.literal: Jiangxia disobeyed my late father's request, truly plotting with Kong Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia disobeyed my late father's request, truly plotting with Kong Jin.

sentences.zh: 天命有歸，故事業不遂耳。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate had its return; thus the enterprise did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate had its return; thus the enterprise did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 夫唯聖人，乃知天命，守忠之臣，唯知盡死，安顧成敗。

translations.literal: Only the sage knows Heaven's mandate; the loyal minister knows only giving full death—how would he care for success or failure?
translations.idiomatic: Only the sage knows Heaven's mandate; the loyal minister knows only giving full death—how would he care for success or failure?

sentences.zh: 詔稱江夏遭時屯故，迹屈行令，內恕探情，無玷純節。

translations.literal: The edict says Jiangxia met the times' hardship, his traces bent to carry out orders, inwardly forgiving and probing feeling, without stain to pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The edict says Jiangxia met the times' hardship, his traces bent to carry out orders, inwardly forgiving and probing feeling, without stain to pure integrity.

sentences.zh: 今茲之旨，又何以處鎮軍哉？
