translations.literal: Now with this intent, how is the Commander to be treated?
translations.idiomatic: Now with this intent, how is the Commander to be treated?

sentences.zh: 臣所言畢矣，乞就湯鑊。

translations.literal: Your servant's words are finished; I beg to approach the boiling cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's words are finished; I beg to approach the boiling cauldron.

sentences.zh: 然臣雖萬沒，猶願陛下必申先臣。

translations.literal: Yet though your servant merits ten thousand deaths, your servant still wishes Your Majesty will surely declare my late father.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though your servant merits ten thousand deaths, your servant still wishes Your Majesty will surely declare my late father.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 惻愴而申之，則天下伏；

translations.literal: Declare him with compassion and the realm will submit;
translations.idiomatic: Declare him with compassion and the realm will submit;

sentences.zh: 不惻愴而申之，天下之人北面而事陛下者，徒以力屈耳。

translations.literal: declare him without compassion and those north of the realm who serve Your Majesty serve only because force has bent them.
translations.idiomatic: declare him without compassion and those who face north to serve Your Majesty serve only because force has bent them.

sentences.zh: 先臣之忠，有識所知，南史之筆，千載可期，亦何待陛下屈申而爲褒貶。

translations.literal: My late father's loyalty is known to those with understanding; the Southern Historian's brush, a thousand years can await it—why wait for Your Majesty to bend and declare for praise or blame?
translations.idiomatic: My late father's loyalty is known to those with understanding; the Southern Historian's brush can await a thousand years—why wait for Your Majesty to bend and declare for praise or blame?

sentences.zh: 然小臣惓惓之愚，爲陛下計耳。

translations.literal: Yet your servant's earnest foolishness is calculated for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your servant's earnest foolishness is calculated for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣之所言，非孝於父，實忠於君。

translations.literal: What your servant speaks is not filial to father but truly loyal to ruler.
translations.idiomatic: What your servant speaks is not filial to father but truly loyal to ruler.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下孰察，少留心焉。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine closely and give a little heed.
translations.idiomatic: Only may Your Majesty examine closely and give a little heed.

sentences.zh: 臣頻觸宸嚴，而不彰露，所以每上封事者，非自爲戇地，猶以春秋之義有隱諱之意也。

translations.literal: Your servant repeatedly touched the imperial countenance yet it was not revealed—therefore each time submitting sealed memorials: not from your servant's own rashness but because the Spring and Autumn principle has the meaning of concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant repeatedly touched the imperial countenance yet it was not revealed—therefore each sealed memorial: not from rashness but because the Spring and Autumn principle has the meaning of concealment.

sentences.zh: 臣雖淺薄，然今日之事，斬足斷頭，殘身滅形，何所不能，爲陛下耳。

translations.literal: Though your servant is shallow, yet in today's affair—cutting foot, severing head, maiming body, extinguishing form—what could I not do, for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Though your servant is shallow, yet in today's affair—cutting foot, severing head, maiming body, extinguishing form—what could I not do, for Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 臣聞生人之死，肉人之骨，有識之士，未爲多感。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that giving life to the dead and flesh to the bone—men with understanding do not deem it excessive feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that giving life to the dead and flesh to the bone—men with understanding do not deem it excessive feeling.

sentences.zh: 公聽竝觀，申人之冤，秉德任公，理人之屈，則普天之人，爭爲之死。

translations.literal: Listen publicly and view together, declare men's wrongs, hold virtue and employ the public, straighten men's bends—then all under Heaven will contend to die.
translations.idiomatic: Listen publicly and view together, declare men's wrongs, hold virtue and employ the public, straighten men's bends—then all under Heaven will contend to die.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 理之所不可以已也。

translations.literal: Because principle cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Because principle cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 陛下若引臣冤，免臣兄之罪，收往失，發惻愴之詔，懷可報之意，則桀之犬實可吠堯，跖之客實可刺由，又何況由之犬，堯之客。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will take up your servant's wrong, pardon your servant's elder brother's crime, gather past losses, issue a compassionate edict, harbor intent that can be repaid—then Jie's dog could truly bark at Yao, Zhi's guest could truly stab You—how much more You's dog and Yao's guest.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will take up your servant's wrong, pardon your servant's elder brother's crime, gather past losses, issue a compassionate edict, harbor intent that can be repaid—then Jie's dog could bark at Yao, Zhi's guest could stab You—how much more You's dog and Yao's guest.

sentences.zh: 臣非生，實爲陛下重此名於天下。

translations.literal: Your servant does not live for himself but truly for Your Majesty to weight this name in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant does not live for himself but truly for Your Majesty to weight this name in the realm.

sentences.zh: 已成之基，可惜之寶，莫復是加。

translations.literal: The foundation already completed, the treasure to be cherished—nothing more can be added.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation already completed, the treasure to be cherished—nothing more can be added.

sentences.zh: 寖明寖昌，不可不循，寖微寖滅，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Growing bright, growing prosperous—this cannot be neglected; growing dim, growing extinct—this cannot be careless.
translations.idiomatic: Growing bright, growing prosperous—this cannot be neglected; growing dim, growing extinct—this cannot be careless.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下熟察，詳擇其衷。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine closely and choose the center in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Only may Your Majesty examine closely and choose the center in detail.

sentences.zh: 若陛下猶以爲疑，鎮軍未之允決，乞下征東共詳可否，無以向隅之悲，而傷陛下滿堂之樂。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty still holds doubt and the Commander has not yet permitted decision, beg to send down the Eastern Campaign to discuss together whether it may be done—do not let the grief of facing the corner wound Your Majesty's joy of a full hall.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty still holds doubt and the Commander has not yet decided, beg to send down the Eastern Campaign to discuss together whether it may be done—do not let grief facing the corner wound Your Majesty's joy of a full hall.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 陛下昏主之弟，江夏亦昏主之弟；

translations.literal: Your Majesty is the muddled ruler's younger brother; Jiangxia is also the muddled ruler's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is the muddled ruler's younger brother; Jiangxia is also the muddled ruler's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 鎮軍受遺託之恩，先臣亦荷顧命之重。

translations.literal: the Commander received the grace of entrustment at death; my late father also bore the weight of dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: the Commander received the grace of deathbed entrustment; my late father also bore the weight of dying charge.

sentences.zh: 情節無異，所爲皆同，殊者唯以成敗仰資聖朝耳。

translations.literal: Sentiment and circumstance are not different; what each did is the same—the only difference is that success and failure rely on the holy court.
translations.idiomatic: Sentiment and circumstance are not different; what each did is the same—the only difference is that success and failure rely on the holy court.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝愚忠，請使羣臣廷辯者，臣乞專令一人，精賜本語。

translations.literal: Your servant cannot overcome foolish loyalty and begs to have the ministers debate at court—your servant begs to be sent alone, finely granted the original words.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cannot overcome foolish loyalty and begs to have the ministers debate at court—your servant begs to be sent alone, finely granted the original words.

sentences.zh: 僥幸萬一，天聽昭然，則軻沈七族，離燔妻子，人以爲難，臣豈不易。

translations.literal: By the slightest chance of ten thousand to one, if Heaven's hearing is bright, then Ke's seven clans drowned, Li's wife and children burned—men think it hard, yet would your servant not find it easy?
translations.idiomatic: By the slightest chance of ten thousand to one, if Heaven's hearing is bright, then Ke's seven clans drowned, Li's wife and children burned—men think it hard, yet would your servant not find it easy?

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「具卿冤切之懷。

translations.literal: The edict replied: "I have fully received your earnest plea of wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "I have fully received your earnest plea of wrong.

sentences.zh: 卿門首義，而旌德未彰，亦追以慨然，今當顯加贈謚。」

translations.literal: Your clan took the lead in righteousness yet virtue was not displayed—this also pursues me with sighing; now posthumous honor will be clearly added."
translations.idiomatic: Your clan took the lead in righteousness yet virtue was not displayed—this also pursues me with sighing; now posthumous honor will be clearly added."

sentences.zh: 偃尋下獄死。

translations.literal: Yan soon went down to prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan soon went down to prison and died.

sentences.zh: 張欣泰字義亨，竟陵人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xintai, style Yihang, was a man of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xintai, whose style name was Yihang, was a native of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 父興世，宋左衞將軍。

translations.literal: His father Xingshi was Song General of the Left Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingshi was a Song General of the Left Wei.

sentences.zh: 欣泰少有志節，不以武業自居，好隷書，讀子史。

translations.literal: Xintai in youth had will and integrity, did not take martial achievement as his station, loved clerical script, and read the histories.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai in youth had will and integrity, did not take martial achievement as his station, loved clerical script, and read the histories.

sentences.zh: 年十餘，詣吏部尚書褚淵，淵問之曰：「張郎弓馬多少。」

translations.literal: When more than ten years old he visited Minister of Personnel Chu Yuan; Yuan asked him: "Young Master Zhang, how much bow and horse?"
translations.idiomatic: When more than ten years old he visited Minister of Personnel Chu Yuan; Yuan asked him: "Young Master Zhang, how much bow and horse?"

sentences.zh: 欣泰答曰：「性怯畏馬，無力牽弓。」

translations.literal: Xintai answered: "By nature I fear horses and have no strength to draw a bow."
translations.idiomatic: Xintai answered: "By nature I fear horses and have no strength to draw a bow."

sentences.zh: 淵甚異之。

translations.literal: Yuan found him very unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan found him very unusual.

sentences.zh: 辟州主簿，歷諸王府佐。

translations.literal: He was summoned as provincial chief clerk and passed through various princes' staff posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as provincial chief clerk and passed through various princes' staff posts.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，興世在家，擁雍州還資，見錢三千萬。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era Xingshi was at home, holding Yong province's returned assets, with cash seen at thirty million.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era Xingshi was at home, holding Yong province's returned assets, with cash seen at thirty million.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王自領人劫之，一夜垂盡，興世憂懼感病卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Cangwu personally led men to rob it; in one night it was nearly gone; Xingshi in worry and fear fell ill and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cangwu personally led men to rob it; in one night it was nearly gone; Xingshi in worry and fear fell ill and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 欣泰兄欣華時任安成郡，欣泰悉封餘財以待之。

translations.literal: Xintai's elder brother Xinhua then held Ancheng commandery; Xintai sealed all remaining wealth to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai's elder brother Xinhua then held Ancheng commandery; Xintai sealed all remaining wealth to await him.

sentences.zh: 建元初，歷官寧朔將軍，累除尚書都官郎。

translations.literal: In the early Jianyuan period he passed through posts to General Who Pacifies the North, and in successive removals became Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jianyuan period he passed through posts to General Who Pacifies the North, and in successive removals became Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 世祖與欣泰早經款遇，及卽位，以爲直閤將軍，領禁旅。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu and Xintai had long been on warm terms; when he took the throne he made him Direct Attendant General overseeing the forbidden guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu and Xintai had long been on warm terms; when he took the throne he made him Direct Attendant General overseeing the forbidden guard.

sentences.zh: 除豫章王太尉參軍，出爲安遠護軍、武陵內史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal Adviser to the Prince of Yuzhang and went out as Protecting Army of Pacifying the Far and Interior Minister of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Marshal Adviser to the Prince of Yuzhang and went out as Protecting Army of Pacifying the Far and Interior Minister of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 還復爲直閤，步兵校尉，領羽林監。

translations.literal: Returning he again became Direct Attendant, Colonel of Footsoldiers, overseeing the Feathered Forest guard.
translations.idiomatic: Returning he again became Direct Attendant, Colonel of Footsoldiers, overseeing the Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 欣泰通涉雅俗，交結多是名素。

translations.literal: Xintai ranged through refined and common circles; his associations were mostly men of established reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai ranged through refined and common circles; his associations were mostly men of established reputation.

sentences.zh: 下直輙遊園池，著鹿皮冠，衲衣錫杖，挾素琴。

translations.literal: Off duty he would roam gardens and pools, wearing a deer-skin cap, patched robe and tin staff, carrying a plain zither.
translations.idiomatic: Off duty he would roam gardens and pools, wearing a deer-skin cap, patched robe and tin staff, carrying a plain zither.

sentences.zh: 有以啓世祖者，世祖曰：「將家兒何敢作此舉止！」

translations.literal: Someone reported this to Emperor Wu; the emperor said: "How dare a general's son make such conduct!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported this to Emperor Wu; the emperor said: "How dare a general's son make such conduct!"

sentences.zh: 後從車駕出新林，敕欣泰甲仗廉察，欣泰停仗，於松樹下飲酒賦詩。

translations.literal: Later following the imperial carriage out to Xinlin, he ordered Xintai to inspect arms and equipment; Xintai halted his weapons, drank wine under a pine tree, and composed poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Later following the imperial carriage out to Xinlin, he ordered Xintai to inspect arms and equipment; Xintai halted his weapons, drank wine under a pine tree, and composed poetry.

sentences.zh: 制局監呂文度過見，啓世祖。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Regulations Lü Wendu passed and saw him and reported to Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of Regulations Lü Wendu passed and saw him and reported to Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 世祖大怒，遣出外，數日，意稍釋，召還，謂之曰：「卿不樂爲武職驅使，當處卿以清貫。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was greatly angered and sent him out; after several days his mind eased somewhat, recalled him, and said: "You do not enjoy being driven in martial service— I shall place you in a pure, honored post."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was greatly angered and sent him out; after several days his mind eased somewhat, recalled him, and said: "You do not enjoy being driven in martial service—I shall place you in a pure, honored post."

sentences.zh: 除正員郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，出爲鎮軍中兵參軍、南平內史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming he went out as Middle Army Adviser to the Pacifying Army and Interior Minister of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming he went out as Middle Army Adviser to the Pacifying Army and Interior Minister of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 巴東王子響殺僚佐，上遣中庶子胡諧之西討，使欣泰爲副。

translations.literal: The Prince of Badong Zixiang killed his staff; the emperor sent Palace Attendant Hu Xiezhi on a western campaign and made Xintai his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Badong Zixiang killed his staff; the emperor sent Palace Attendant Hu Xiezhi on a western campaign and made Xintai his deputy.

sentences.zh: 欣泰謂諧之曰：「今太歲在西南，逆歲行軍，兵家深忌，不可見戰，戰必見危。

translations.literal: Xintai told Xiezhi: "Now the Grand Year is in the southwest; marching against the year is what military families deeply fear—you must not see battle; if you see battle you will surely meet peril.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai told Xiezhi: "Now the Grand Year is in the southwest; marching against the year is what military families deeply fear—you must not see battle; if you see battle you will surely meet peril.

sentences.zh: 今假此行，勝旣無名，負誠可恥。

translations.literal: Now borrowing this march—if victorious there is no fame, if defeated it is truly shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Now borrowing this march—if victorious there is no fame, if defeated it is truly shameful.

sentences.zh: 彼凶狡相聚，所以爲其用者，或利賞逼威，無由自潰。

translations.literal: Those fierce and cunning who gather—what makes them usable is sometimes profit and reward or forced authority; they cannot dissolve of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Those fierce and cunning who gather—what makes them usable is sometimes profit and reward or forced authority; they cannot dissolve of themselves.

sentences.zh: 若且頓軍夏口，宣示禍福，可不戰而禽也。」

translations.literal: If we halt the army at Xiakou and proclaim fortune and calamity, we may take them without battle."
translations.idiomatic: If we halt the army at Xiakou and proclaim fortune and calamity, we may take them without battle."

sentences.zh: 諧之不從，進屯江津，尹略等見殺。

translations.literal: Xiezhi did not follow; advanced and encamped at Jinjin; Yin Lue and others were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi did not follow; advanced and encamped at Jinjin; Yin Lue and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 事平，欣泰徙爲隨王子隆鎮西中兵，改領河東內史。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled Xintai was moved to Western Army Adviser to the Prince of Sui and changed to oversee Interior Minister of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled Xintai was moved to Western Army Adviser to the Prince of Sui and changed to oversee Interior Minister of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 子隆深相愛納，數與談宴，州府職局，多使關領，意遇與謝朓相次。

translations.literal: Zilong deeply loved and received him, often talking and feasting with him; many posts of the province and prefecture he had oversee—his favor ranked next after Xie Tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong deeply loved and received him, often talking and feasting with him; many posts of the province and prefecture he had oversee—his favor ranked next after Xie Tiao.

sentences.zh: 典籤密以啓聞，世祖怒，召還都。

translations.literal: The registrar secretly reported this; Emperor Wu was angry and recalled him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar secretly reported this; Emperor Wu was angry and recalled him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 屏居家巷，置宅南岡下，面接松山。

translations.literal: He secluded himself in his home lane and set a residence below the southern ridge, facing Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He secluded himself in his home lane and set a residence below the southern ridge, facing Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 欣泰負弩射雉，恣情閑放。

translations.literal: Xintai shouldered a crossbow to shoot pheasants and indulged in idle freedom.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai shouldered a crossbow to shoot pheasants and indulged in idle freedom.

sentences.zh: 衆伎雜藝，頗多閑解。

translations.literal: Among many performing arts he was quite skilled in leisurely pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: Among many performing arts he was quite skilled in leisurely pursuits.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，爲領軍長史，遷諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was Chief Clerk to the Palace Army and moved to Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was Chief Clerk to the Palace Army and moved to Adviser.

sentences.zh: 上書陳便宜二十條，其一條言宜毀廢塔寺。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial stating twenty items of practical benefit; one item said pagodas and temples should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial stating twenty items of practical benefit; one item said pagodas and temples should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 帝竝優詔報答。

translations.literal: The emperor with all gave favorable edicts in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor with all gave favorable edicts in reply.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，虜圍鍾離城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu the barbarians besieged Zhongli city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu the barbarians besieged Zhongli city.

sentences.zh: 欣泰爲軍主，隨崔慧景救援。

translations.literal: Xintai was army commander and followed Cui Huijing in the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai was army commander and followed Cui Huijing in the rescue.

sentences.zh: 欣泰移虜廣陵侯曰：「聞攻鍾離，是子之深策，可無謬哉！

translations.literal: Xintai sent word to the barbarians' Prince of Guangling: "I hear you attack Zhongli—that is your deep strategy; can it be without error!
translations.idiomatic: Xintai sent word to the barbarians' Prince of Guangling: "I hear you attack Zhongli—that is your deep strategy; can it be without error!

sentences.zh: 《兵法》云『城有所不攻，地有所不爭』。

translations.literal: The Art of War says "there are cities one does not attack, lands one does not contend for."
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War says "there are cities one does not attack, lands one does not contend for."

sentences.zh: 豈不聞之乎？

translations.literal: Have you not heard it?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not heard it?

sentences.zh: 我國家舟舸百萬，覆江橫海，所以案甲于今不至，欲以邊城疲魏士卒。

translations.literal: Our state's boats and ships number a million, covering the river and crossing the sea—therefore we keep armor on till now and have not come, wishing to wear out Wei's soldiers on the frontier city.
translations.idiomatic: Our state's boats and ships number a million, covering the river and crossing the sea—therefore we keep armor on till now and have not come, wishing to wear out Wei's soldiers on the frontier city.

sentences.zh: 我且千里運糧，行留俱弊，一時霖雨，川谷涌溢，然後乘帆渡海，百萬齊進，子復奚以御之？

translations.literal: We yet transport grain a thousand li, going and staying both exhausted; once sudden rain for days, streams and valleys overflow—then riding sails to cross the sea, a million advance together—what will you use to resist?
translations.idiomatic: We yet transport grain a thousand li, going and staying both exhausted; once sudden rain for days, streams and valleys overflow—then riding sails to cross the sea, a million advance together—what will you use to resist?

sentences.zh: 乃令魏主以萬乘之重，攻此小城，是何謂歟？

translations.literal: Yet you make the Wei lord with the weight of ten thousand chariots attack this little city—what does that mean?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you make the Wei lord with the weight of ten thousand chariots attack this little city—what does that mean?

sentences.zh: 攻而不拔，誰之恥邪？

translations.literal: If you attack and cannot take it—whose shame would that be?
translations.idiomatic: If you attack yet cannot take the city—whose shame is that?

sentences.zh: 假令能拔，子守之，我將連舟千里，舳艫相屬，西過壽陽，東接滄海，仗不再請，糧不更取，士卒偃卧，起而接戰，乃魚鼈不通，飛鳥斷絕，偏師淮左，其不能守，皎可知矣。

translations.literal: Suppose you could take it and you held it—I would link boats for a thousand li, stern to stern, pass west of Shouchun and east to the blue sea, weapons not asked for again, grain not taken again, soldiers lying down then rising to join battle—then fish and turtles would not pass, birds would be cut off; a detached force on the Huai's left could not hold it—that is as clear as day.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose you could take it and held it—I would link boats for a thousand li, sterns touching sterns, pass west of Shouchun and east to the blue sea, ask for no more weapons, take no more grain, let soldiers rest then rise to fight—then fish and turtles would not pass, birds would be cut off; a detached force on the Huai left could not hold—that is as clear as day.

sentences.zh: 如其不拔，吾將假法于魏之有司，以請子之過。

translations.literal: If you cannot take it, I shall borrow the law from Wei's officials to request your fault.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot take it, I shall invoke the law through Wei's officials to demand an accounting of your fault.

sentences.zh: 若挫兵夷衆，攻不卒下，驅士填隍，拔而不能守，則魏朝名士，其當別有深致乎，吾所未能量。

translations.literal: If you break your troops and flatten your host, attack yet do not take it quickly, drive men to fill the moat, take yet cannot hold—then do the famed gentlemen of Wei's court have some deeper meaning I have not yet measured?
translations.idiomatic: If you break your troops and flatten your host, attack yet fail to take it quickly, drive men to fill the moat, capture yet cannot hold—then do Wei's court gentlemen have some deeper design I have not yet fathomed?

sentences.zh: 昔魏之太武佛狸，傾一國之衆，攻十雉之城，死亡太半，僅以身返。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei's Emperor Taiwu Fotu, bending the host of a whole state, attacked a city of ten perches—more than half died and he returned with only his body.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Wei's Emperor Taiwu Fotu bent the host of a whole state to attack a ten-perch city—more than half died and he returned with only his body.

sentences.zh: 旣智屈於金墉，亦雖拔而不守，皆筭失所爲，至今爲笑。

translations.literal: His wisdom was bent at Jinyong; though he took it he could not hold it—both were calculations that missed their mark and are laughter to this day.
translations.idiomatic: His wits were exhausted at Jinyong; though he took it he could not hold it—both were plans that missed their mark and are mocked to this day.

sentences.zh: 前鑒未遠，已忘之乎？

translations.literal: The mirror before is not far—have you already forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: The lesson before you is not far—have you already forgotten?

sentences.zh: 和門邑邑，戲載往意。」

translations.literal: Harmony at the gate, the district at ease—I playfully carry my former intent."
translations.idiomatic: Harmony at the gate, the district at ease—I playfully bear my former intent."

sentences.zh: 虜旣爲徐州軍所挫，更欲於邵陽洲築城。

translations.literal: The barbarians having been checked by the Xuzhou army wished again to build a city on Shaoyang Isle.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians, having been checked by the Xuzhou army, wished again to build a city on Shaoyang Isle.

sentences.zh: 慧景慮爲大患。

translations.literal: Huijing feared it would become a great peril.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing feared it would become a grave peril.

sentences.zh: 欣泰曰：「虜所以築城者，外示姱大，實懼我躡其後耳。

translations.literal: Xintai said: "The reason the barbarians build a city is outwardly to show grandeur; in truth they fear we will tread on their heels.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai said: "The barbarians build a city to show grandeur outwardly; in truth they fear we will tread on their heels.

sentences.zh: 今若說之以彼此各願罷兵，則其患自息。」

translations.literal: If we now persuade them that both sides wish to cease arms, their peril will quiet of itself."
translations.idiomatic: If we now persuade them that both sides wish to lay down arms, their trouble will quiet of itself."

sentences.zh: 慧景從之。

translations.literal: Huijing followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 遣欣泰至虜城下具述此意。

translations.literal: He sent Xintai to the barbarian city wall to state this intent fully.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xintai to the foot of the barbarian wall to state this intent in full.

sentences.zh: 及虜引退，而洲上餘兵萬人，求輸五百匹馬假道，慧景欲斷路攻之。

translations.literal: When the barbarians withdrew, more than ten thousand remaining troops on the isle requested five hundred horses to pass through by borrowed road; Huijing wished to cut the road and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians withdrew, more than ten thousand remaining troops on the isle requested five hundred horses to pass through on loan; Huijing wished to cut the road and attack them.

sentences.zh: 欣泰說慧景曰：「歸師勿遏，古人畏之。

translations.literal: Xintai urged Huijing: "Do not block a returning army—the ancients feared this.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai urged Huijing: "Do not block a returning army—the ancients feared this.

sentences.zh: 死地之兵，不可輕也。

translations.literal: Troops in dead ground must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers caught in dead ground must not be slighted.

sentences.zh: 勝之旣不足爲武，敗則徒喪前功。

translations.literal: Victory would not suffice for martial glory; defeat would only waste the prior achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Victory would not suffice for martial glory; defeat would only waste the prior achievement.

sentences.zh: 不如許之。」

translations.literal: Better to permit them."
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to let them pass."

sentences.zh: 慧景乃聽虜過。

translations.literal: Huijing then allowed the barbarians to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing thereupon let the barbarians pass.

sentences.zh: 時領軍蕭坦之亦援鍾離，還啓明帝曰：「邵陽洲有死賊萬人，慧景、欣泰放而不取。」

translations.literal: At that time Palace Army Leader Xiao Tanzhi also aided Zhongli; returning he reported to Emperor Ming: "On Shaoyang Isle are ten thousand doomed bandits—Huijing and Xintai released them and did not take them."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Army Leader Xiao Tanzhi also aided Zhongli; returning he reported to Emperor Ming: "On Shaoyang Isle are ten thousand doomed bandits—Huijing and Xintai released them and did not take them."

sentences.zh: 帝以此皆不加賞。

translations.literal: The emperor on this account gave neither reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor on this account gave neither man a reward.

sentences.zh: 四年，出爲永陽太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out as Prefect of Yongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was sent out as Prefect of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 永元初，還都。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongyuan he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongyuan he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景圍城，欣泰入城內，領軍守備。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing besieged the city Xintai entered within the walls; the Palace Army Leader held the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing besieged the city, Xintai entered within the walls; the Palace Army Leader held the defense.

sentences.zh: 事寧，除輔國將軍、廬陵王安東司馬。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Pacifying East Chief Clerk to the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Pacifying East Chief Clerk to the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 義師起，以欣泰爲持節、督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、雍州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the army of righteousness rose Xintai was made bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in the four provinces Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Jingling district of Yingzhou, and Sui commandery of Sizhou, and Inspector of Yong—general as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the army of righteousness rose, Xintai was made bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, the Jingling district of Yingzhou, and the Sui commandery of Sizhou, and Inspector of Yong—general as before.

sentences.zh: 時少帝昏亂，人情咸伺事隙。

translations.literal: At that time the young emperor was muddled and chaotic; popular sentiment everywhere watched for an opening in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the young emperor was muddled and chaotic; popular sentiment everywhere watched for an opening in affairs.

sentences.zh: 欣泰與弟前始安內史欣時密謀結太子右率胡松、前南譙太守王靈秀、直閤將軍鴻選、含德主帥苟勵、直後劉靈運等十餘人，竝同契會。

translations.literal: Xintai with his younger brother the former Interior Minister of Shian Xinshi secretly plotted to join Right Leader of the Heir Apparent Hu Song, former Prefect of Nanqiao Wang Lingxiu, Direct Attendant General Hong Xuan, Hande garrison commander Gou Li, Direct Rear Liu Lingyun, and more than ten others—all pledged together.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai with his younger brother the former Interior Minister of Shian Xinshi secretly plotted to join Right Leader of the Heir Apparent Hu Song, former Prefect of Nanqiao Wang Lingxiu, Direct Attendant General Hong Xuan, Hande garrison commander Gou Li, Direct Rear Liu Lingyun, and more than ten others—all pledged together.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中書舍人馮元嗣監軍救郢，茹法珍、梅蟲兒及太子右率李居士、制局監楊明泰等十餘人相送中興堂。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Attendant of the Central Secretariat Feng Yuansi to oversee the army rescuing Ying; Ru Fazhen, Mei Chonger, and Right Leader of the Heir Apparent Li Jushi, Supervisor of Regulations Yang Mingtai, and more than ten others escorted them to the Zhongxing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Attendant of the Central Secretariat Feng Yuansi to oversee the army rescuing Ying; Ru Fazhen, Mei Chonger, Right Leader of the Heir Apparent Li Jushi, Supervisor of Regulations Yang Mingtai, and more than ten others escorted them to the Zhongxing Hall.

sentences.zh: 欣泰等使人懷刀於座斫元嗣，頭墜果柈中，又斫明泰，破其腹，蟲兒傷刺數瘡，手指皆墮。

translations.literal: Xintai and others had men with knives in their bosoms at the seats chop Yuansi; his head fell into the fruit tray; they also chopped Mingtai and broke open his belly; Chonger was wounded with several stabs and all his fingers fell off.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai and others had men with knives at the seats chop Yuansi; his head fell into the fruit tray. They also chopped Mingtai and broke open his belly; Chonger was stabbed several times and all his fingers fell off.

sentences.zh: 居士踰牆得出，茹法珍亦散走還臺。

translations.literal: Jushi climbed the wall and got out; Ru Fazhen also scattered in flight back to the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Jushi climbed the wall and escaped; Ru Fazhen also scattered in flight back to the terrace.

sentences.zh: 靈秀仍往石頭迎建安王寶夤，率文武數百，唱警蹕，至杜姥宅。

translations.literal: Lingxiu then went to Stone Fortress to welcome the Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin, leading several hundred civil and military men, proclaiming the imperial guard, and came to Old Du's house.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxiu then went to Stone Fortress to welcome the Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin, leading several hundred civil and military men, proclaiming the imperial guard, and came to Old Du's house.

sentences.zh: 欣泰初聞事發，馳馬入宮，冀法珍等在外，城內處分，必盡見委，表裏相應，因行廢立。

translations.literal: When Xintai first heard the affair had broken out he galloped into the palace, hoping Fazhen and others were outside and that disposition within the city would surely entrust everything to him—inside and outside responding together—thereby carrying out deposition and establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Xintai first heard the affair had broken out he galloped into the palace, hoping Fazhen and others were outside and that disposition within the city would entrust everything to him—inside and outside responding together—thereby carrying out deposition and establishment.

sentences.zh: 旣而法珍得反，處分閉門上仗，不配欣泰兵，鴻選在殿內亦不敢發。

translations.literal: Soon Fazhen got back, disposed matters, shut the gates and posted weapons, did not assign troops to Xintai's men, and Hong Xuan within the hall also did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fazhen returned, took command, shut the gates and posted weapons, did not assign troops to Xintai's men, and Hong Xuan within the hall also did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 城外衆尋散。

translations.literal: The host outside soon scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The forces outside the city soon dispersed.

sentences.zh: 少日事覺，詔收欣泰、胡松等，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Within a few days the affair was discovered; an edict seized Xintai, Hu Song, and others—all were executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the affair was discovered; an edict seized Xintai, Hu Song, and others—all were executed by law.

sentences.zh: 欣泰少時有人相其當得三公，而年裁三十。

translations.literal: When Xintai was young someone physiognomized him saying he would attain the three excellencies while only thirty years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Xintai was young someone physiognomized him and said he would attain the three excellencies while only thirty years old.

sentences.zh: 後屋瓦墮傷額，又問相者，云：「無復公相，年壽更增，亦可得方伯耳。」

translations.literal: Later a roof tile fell and wounded his forehead; he again asked the physiognomist, who said: "No longer the excellency aspect; years of life increase—you may yet obtain a regional lordship."
translations.idiomatic: Later a roof tile fell and wounded his forehead; he again asked the physiognomist, who said: "No longer the aspect of the three excellencies; your years of life increase—you may yet obtain a regional lordship."

sentences.zh: 死時年四十六。

translations.literal: When he died he was forty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：崔慧景宿將老臣，憂危昏運，回董御之威，舉晉陽之甲，乘機用權，內襲少主，因樂亂之民，藉淮楚之剽，驍將授首，羣帥委律，鼓鼙讙於宮寢，戈戟跱於城隍，陵埤負戶，士衰氣竭，屢發銅虎之兵，未有釋位之援，勢等易京，魚爛待盡。

translations.literal: The historian says: Cui Huijing, an old general of long service, in peril of a muddled age turned Dong Yu's authority and raised the armor of Jinyang, seized the moment and used power, struck inward at the young emperor, relied on people who delighted in chaos, borrowed the fierceness of Huai and Chu—valiant generals surrendered their heads, group commanders cast away discipline; drums and gongs rejoiced in the palace chambers, spears and halberds stood in the city walls; bearing households on the ramparts, soldiers' spirits failed and breath exhausted; repeatedly issuing bronze-tiger troops yet no relief that released position—situation equal to Yijing, fish rotting awaiting the end.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Cui Huijing, an old general of long service, facing the peril of a muddled age turned Dong Yu's authority and raised the armor of Jinyang. Seizing the moment and wielding power, he struck inward at the young emperor, relied on those who delighted in chaos, and borrowed the fierceness of Huai and Chu. Valiant generals surrendered their heads; group commanders cast away discipline. Drums and gongs sounded in the palace chambers; spears and halberds stood along the city walls. The people bore their households on the ramparts; soldiers' spirits failed and their breath ran out. He repeatedly issued bronze-tiger troops yet found no relief that would release his position—his situation matched Yijing, fish rotting as he awaited the end.

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍投袂以先國急，束馬旅師，橫江競濟，風驅電掃，制勝轉丸，越城之戰，旗獲蔽野，津𦨵之捷，獻俘象魏，瞻塵望烽，窮壘重辟，戮帶定襄，曾未及此。

translations.literal: The Conquering Barbarians General flung his sleeves to put the state's urgency first, bound horses and gathered troops, crossed the river in competing passage—wind driving, lightning sweeping, overcoming as turning a pellet; at the battle of Yuecheng banners and captives covered the wild; at the ford victory captives were offered at the Gate of Bright Law—gazing at dust, watching beacons, exhausting fortresses and doubling passes, executing Dai and settling Xiang—never reached this.
translations.idiomatic: The Conquering Barbarians General flung his sleeves to answer the state's urgency first, bound horses and gathered troops, and crossed the river in competing waves—wind-driven, lightning-swift, victory turning like a pellet in the hand. At the battle of Yuecheng banners and captives covered the wild; at the ford victory captives were offered at the Gate of Bright Law. Gazing at dust, watching beacons, exhausting fortresses and doubling passes, executing Dai and settling Xiang—none of it matched this.

sentences.zh: 盛矣哉，桓文異世也！

translations.literal: Sublime! Huan and Wen in different ages!
translations.idiomatic: How grand it is—Huan and Wen across different ages!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：叔業外叛，淮肥失險。

translations.literal: The praise says: Shuye rebelled outward; Huai and Fei lost their defiles.
translations.idiomatic: The praise says: Shuye rebelled outward; Huai and Fei lost their defiles.

sentences.zh: 慧景倒戈，宮門晝掩。

translations.literal: Huijing turned his spears; palace gates shut by day.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing turned his spears; palace gates were shut by day.

sentences.zh: 欣泰倉卒，霜刃不染。

translations.literal: Xintai in haste—frosted blades unstained.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai acted in haste—frosted blades unstained.

sentences.zh: 實起時昬，堅氷互漸。

translations.literal: Truly the times' muddle arose; hard ice formed layer on layer.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the times' muddle arose; hard ice formed layer on layer.
